declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_certificate_supply (hsupply : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **The wave-21 reduction (the throat of #249).** A certified period-kill supply — for every period `h ≥ 1` and every threshold `N₀`, a certified kill at some `(N ≥ N₀, L)` — proves the totient series irrational. Each individual certificate is a finite, decidable residue computation.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_diagonal_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_diagonal_certificate_supply (hsupply : ∀ t₀ : ℕ, ∃ t, t₀ ≤ t ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **The wave-23 diagonal collapse.** #249 follows from a SINGLE ℕ-indexed sequence of decidable statements: the endpoint certificate firing on the diagonal `(h, N) = (periodLcm t, periodLcm t)` for infinitely many `t`. Rationality would supply a primitive period `h₀` and pre-period `N₀`; any `t ≥ max(h₀, N₀)` gives `h₀ ∣ periodLcm t` and `periodLcm t ≥ t ≥ N₀` simultaneously, so a diagonal kill at such `t` is a contradiction. No second parameter remains.

declarations.name: rational_totient_series_forces_lcm_cone_flatness
declarations.signature: theorem rational_totient_series_forces_lcm_cone_flatness (hrat : ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)) : ∃ t₁ : ℕ, ∀ t, t₁ ≤ t → ∀ q m : ℕ, 0 < q → totientTail (q * periodLcm t + m * periodLcm t) - totientTail (q * periodLcm t) ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **The lcm-cone flatness law.** If the totient series is rational, then from some scale on, the ENTIRE lcm cone is fractionally flat: every difference `R_{q·H_t + m·H_t} - R_{q·H_t}` is an integer, for every `t` past the threshold, every base multiplier `q ≥ 1`, and every step multiplier `m`. One constant fractional part governs every cone point — the maximal spend of the rationality hypothesis on the lcm lattice.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_iff_pointwise_certificates
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_iff_pointwise_certificates : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ↔ ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Certificate completeness turns the pointwise non-integrality normal form into a pointwise finite-receipt normal form.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_iff_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_iff_certificate_supply : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ↔ ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: The wave-21 cofinal certificate supply is not a weaker large-measure surrogate: together with completeness it is exactly equivalent to #249.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_iff_lcm_diagonal_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_iff_lcm_diagonal_certificate_supply : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ↔ ∀ t₀ : ℕ, ∃ t, t₀ ≤ t ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L

In the forward direction, pointwise certificate completeness supplies the diagonal certificate already at `t = t₀`; the reverse direction is the diagonal collapse.

\begin{corollary}[finite residue projection]\label{res:freshloss}
For every \(t,L\in\N\), the diagonal projection certificate is equivalent to
\[
 M_t+L+2<\eta_{t,L}<2^L-(2M_t+L+2),
\]
and either condition forces full-target avoidance at height \(t\).
Consequently,
\[
 \forall t_0\in\N\;\exists t\geq t_0\;\exists L\in\N,\qquad
 M_t+L+2<\eta_{t,L}<2^L-(2M_t+L+2)
\]
implies that \(S\) is irrational.
\end{corollary}

source_excerpt.text:
\paragraph{Candidate unbounded input: a three-rank odd window.}\label{res:flexibleoddwindow}
Fix $t=2^a$ and increase the canonical suffix depth by at most one to write it
as $m=2q+1$.  Call a rank \emph{central} when its half-word residue lies
between $4^q/32$ and $31\cdot4^q/32$.  Test $q,q+1,q+2$; centrality at any one
yields the required adjacent-suffix gap condition,
\lword{DiagonalFlexibleOddWindowSupply.lean}{93}{diagonalAdjacentSuffixGapSupply_of_powerTwoOddGuardThreeRankBand}{three-rank suffix-gap implication}.
Thus success of this three-rank test for arbitrarily large $a$ implies
irrationality,
\lword{DiagonalFlexibleOddWindowSupply.lean}{137}{irrational_totientSeries_of_powerTwoOddGuardThreeRankBandSupply}{unbounded three-rank criterion};
that supply is not proved.

source_excerpt.text:
\paragraph{Exact affine form and bounded zero-orbit obstruction.}\label{res:flexibleoddaffine}
Let $x_q$ be the centred half-word residue and put $e_q=4^q/32$.  Centrality is
$|x_q|\geq e_q$; under the stated bounds on the next two corrections, the three
tests are equivalent to one affine escape disjunction,
\lword{DiagonalFlexibleOddWindowAffine.lean}{236}{threeRankBandAt_iff_threeScaleAffineEscapeAt_of_shortCorrections}{three-scale affine equivalence}.
Yet the generic recurrence $y_{j+1}=4y_j+c_j$, started at zero, can satisfy
$|y_j|<4^j e$ for every $j$ even when every $|c_j|<2e$,
\lword{DiagonalFlexibleOddWindowAffine.lean}{225}{zeroAffineOrbit_stays_in_scaled_edge}{zero-orbit obstruction}.

assertions.label: Exact power-of-two one-bit lift
assertions.statement: Given agreement modulo 2^k, agreement modulo 2^(k+1) is exactly evenness of the signed quotient after division by 2^k; failure gives the unique offset class. In particular, a signed difference 16*c agrees modulo 32 exactly when c is even. Under the stated correction and margin budget, the centered signed-margin socket is exactly failure of this next lift. This provides a finite fifth-bit interface and does not supply cofactor parity at unbounded scales.

declarations.signature: theorem reducedMarginSocket_not_decided_by_parity {m A : ℤ} (hmEven : Even m) (hmPos : 0 < m) (h16A : 16 < A) (hA : A < 8 * m - 16) : (∃ yHit yMiss : ℤ, Even yHit ∧ Even yMiss ∧ ReducedMarginSocket m A yHit ∧ ¬ ReducedMarginSocket m A yMiss) ∧ (∃ yHit yMiss : ℤ, Odd yHit ∧ Odd yMiss ∧ ReducedMarginSocket m A yHit ∧ ¬ ReducedMarginSocket m A yMiss)
declarations.docstring: Knowing only the parity of a reduced quotient cannot decide its margin socket. In each parity class there is both a socket hit and a socket miss. The hits are `0` and `1`. source_excerpt.text:
\begin{proposition}[parity does not decide the reduced margin condition]
\label{res:paritysocket}
Let \(m,a\in\Z\), with \(m>0\) even and
\[
 16<a<8m-16,
\]
and put
\[
 \mathcal M_{m,a}
 =\{y\in\Z:\exists k\in\Z,\ 16|y-km|<a\}.
\]
Each parity class contains both a member and a nonmember of
\(\mathcal M_{m,a}\).  In particular, the conclusion holds for
\(m=2^j\) whenever \(j\geq1\).
\end{proposition}

\label{res:slackcriterion}
If, for every $t_0$, there is a $t\ge\max\{3,t_0\}$ such that

\]
then $S$ is irrational.

\begin{proposition}[finite sufficient test for diagonal nonintegrality]\label{res:foreignresidue}
Let \(F_H^{(D)}\) be the retained nondivisor projection at cutoff \(D\), let
\(F_H\) be the actual foreign defect, and let \(Q_H\) be the scaled explicit
divisor shadow.  The finite residue diagonal is exactly the sum of
\(F_H^{(D)}\) and its divisor-index complement.  For \(2H\leq D\), put
\[
 B_{H,D}=c_H\left(\frac{2}{2^D}+\frac{4}{3\,4^D}\right).
\]
If
\[
 |F_H-F_H^{(D)}|\leq B_{H,D}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 |Q_H+F_H^{(D)}-z|>B_{H,D}\quad\text{for every }z\in\Z,
\]
then the full target at height \(H\) is not attained.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[exact denominator of the M"obius shadow]\label{res:shadowden}
Let \(r_t\) be the square-free kernel of \(M_t\), let \(s_t=M_t/r_t\), and
let \(J(r_t)\) be the odd Jordan scalar.  The reduced denominator \(d_t\) of
the scaled M\"obius shadow is
\[
 d_t=
 \frac{2^{r_t}-1}
 {\gcd\!\bigl(2^{r_t}-1,\,s_t\lvert J(r_t)\rvert\bigr)}.
\]
If \(t\geq5\), then
\[
 \prod_{\substack{p\ \mathrm{prime}\\ t/2<p\leq t}}(2^p-1)
 \ \mid\ d_t,
 \qquad d_t\geq2^{\lfloor t/2\rfloor}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[independent no-go: square-CRT correction suppression]\label{res:squarecrt}
Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite family indexed by distinct primes $p_i$, with prescribed
anchors $A_i$ and residues $a_i$.  There is a bounded common base $n$ such
that, for each $i\in\mathcal E$ and each shift $h$ with $p_i\nmid a_i+h$, one has
\[
 n=A_i+p_i(a_i+p_i t)\quad\text{and}\quad
 \ph(n+p_i h-A_i)=(p_i-1)\ph(a_i+p_i t+h)
\]
for a suitable $t\in\N$.  In particular, if every $p_i$ exceeds a fixed
horizon $J$, the choice $a_i=0$ works simultaneously for all $1\le h\le J$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic basis]\label{res:basis}
The family
\[
 \{\ph_{0,0},\ph_{1,0}\}
 \cup\{\ph_{j,r}:j\ge1,\ 0<r<2^j,\ r\text{ odd}\},
 \qquad \ph_{j,r}(n)=\ph(2^jn+r),
\]
is a basis for the rational span of the full dyadic kernel. Every rational
relation is generated by the scalar reductions. The complete level-zero
truncation has dimension one.
\end{corollary}

declarations.signature: theorem totient_pow_mul_eq (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (n : ℕ) : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → Nat.totient (k ^ j * n) = k ^ (j - 1) * Nat.totient (k * n)
declarations.docstring: The zero-residue relation of the totient `k`-kernel: for `j ≥ 1`, `φ (k^j * n) = k^(j-1) * φ (k * n)`.

declarations.name: totient_pow_mul_affine_gcd_cross_eq
declarations.signature: theorem totient_pow_mul_affine_gcd_cross_eq (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (h n u t : ℕ) (hh : 1 ≤ h) (ht : 1 ≤ t) : Nat.totient (Nat.gcd k u) * Nat.totient (k ^ t * (k ^ h * n + u)) = k ^ (t - 1) * Nat.totient k * Nat.gcd k u * Nat.totient (k ^ h * n + u)
declarations.docstring: Exact affine-section specialization of `totient_pow_mul_gcd_cross_eq`. For `m = k^h n + u` with `h ≥ 1`, the correction factor is controlled by `gcd(k,u)` and is therefore constant along the section. This is the arithmetic layer needed before the finite-dimensional all-base kernel basis argument; it does not assert the remaining linear independence theorem.

declarations.name: card_totientKernelIndex_eq_two_add_sum

declarations.name: allBaseTotientKernelSeq_mul_residue_step
declarations.signature: theorem allBaseTotientKernelSeq_mul_residue_step (k j r : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : allBaseTotientKernelSeq k (j + 1) (k * r) = totientKernelReductionScalar k r • allBaseTotientKernelSeq k j r

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[exact rank of every totient $k$-kernel truncation]
\label{thm:kkernelrank}
Let $k\ge2$ and $e\ge1$ be integers, write $F^{(k)}_{j,r}(n)=\ph(k^jn+r)$, and put
\[
 V_{k,e}=\operatorname{span}_{\Q}
 \{\,F^{(k)}_{j,r}:0\le j\le e,\ 0\le r<k^j\,\}.
\]
Then $\dim_{\Q}V_{k,e}=k^e+1$, and
\[
 \mathcal B_{k,e}
 =\{F^{(k)}_{0,0},F^{(k)}_{1,0}\}
 \cup\{\,F^{(k)}_{j,r}:1\le j\le e,\ 1\le r<k^j,\ k\nmid r\,\}
\]
is a basis.  Every omitted section reduces to a basis element by an explicit
scalar: $F^{(k)}_{j,0}=k^{j-1}F^{(k)}_{1,0}$ for $j\ge1$, and if $r=k^tu$ with
$t=\max\{s:k^s\mid r\}\ge1$ and $k\nmid u$, then
\[
 F^{(k)}_{j,r}=C_k(t,u)\,F^{(k)}_{j-t,u},
 \qquad
 C_k(t,u)=k^t\prod_{\substack{p\mid k\\ p\nmid u}}\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

assertions.statement: For a residual-weighted monomial matrix, common nonzero residual weights act by a right diagonal gauge and preserve determinant nonvanishing. Under the locked inverse-phase gauge, an exponent-one row is identically 1 even when the determinant remains nonzero; allowing row-dependent residuals reconstructs a consecutive-power matrix with zeroth row identically 1. \begin{proposition}[column-rescaling obstruction for monomial minors]\label{res:residualgauge}
Let $z_j,W_j\ne0$ and $M_{ij}=W_jz_j^{e_i}$.  Then
\(det M=\det(z_j^{e_i})\prod_jW_j\), so the column weights preserve
determinant nonvanishing.  If $e_i=1$, choosing $W_j=z_j^{-1}$ makes row $i$
identically $1$.  Allowing row-dependent weights
$W_{ij}=z_j^i/z_j^{e_i}$ reconstructs a consecutive-power matrix whose
zeroth row is identically $1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[support fraction--Boolean-carry equivalence]\label{res:carrycert}
Fix $p\in\mathbb Z$ and an integer $q\ge1$. There is a nonempty support $A$ of
positive integers with $\sum_{n\in A}1/(2^n-1)=p/q$ if and only if there is an
integer sequence $U$, with $U(0)=p$, such that, for every $N$,
\[
  0<U(N)\le q\,(2\sqrt N+4)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  q\mid 2U(N)-U(N+1),
\]
and the M\"obius transform of the quotient sequence
$N\mapsto\bigl(2U(N)-U(N+1)\bigr)/q$ is Boolean. The support is not guessed:
it is reconstructed from the certificate by Proposition~\ref{res:boolmob}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[order-wrap lower bound, with exact excess mean]\label{res:orderwrap}
Let \(A\subseteq\Npos\) be nonempty and suppose
\[
 X_A=\frac{p}{2^cv},
 \qquad p\in\Z,\quad c\in\N,\quad v>1\ \text{odd}.
\]
Let \(h=\operatorname{ord}_v(2)\), let \(w\) be the number of wraps in the
least-residue cycle \(p2^N\bmod v\) for \(0\leq N<h\), and set
\[
 u(N)=vT_{f_A}(c+N),\qquad e_N=\left\lfloor\frac{u(N)}v\right\rfloor.
\]
Then $\sum_{a\in A}1/a$ diverges or $\rho(A)\ge w/h$; if moreover $p$ is
coprime to $v$, then $w\ge1$, so
$\rho(A)\ge1/\operatorname{ord}_v(2)$. In the summable case the bound is the
periodic part of an exact identity: the Ces\`aro mean of \(e_N\) converges,
and
\[
\rho(A)\;=\;\frac{w}{h}\;+\;\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{n<N}e_n .
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[sublogarithmic zero windows]\label{res:sublog}
Let $A$ contain a positive integer and suppose
\[
  \sum_{a\in A}\frac1{2^a-1}=\frac{p}{2^c v},
  \qquad p\in\Z,\quad c\in\N,\quad v\ge1.
\]
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $B\ge0$, depending only on
$\varepsilon,c,$ and $v$, such that every zero window after $c+N$ satisfies
\[
  h\le \varepsilon\log_2(N+1)+B,
  \qquad \log_2 x:=\frac{\log x}{\log 2}.
\]
The bound is uniform in $A,p,N,$ and $h$.
\end{theorem}

assertions.label: Exact band localization of the final skip between two takes
assertions.statement: Suppose a take at rank b is followed by the next take at c > b+1, put q = 2^b − 1 and m = 2^(c−1), and write the pre-take residual as 1/R with 0 < R < q. The final intervening skip is dyadically unsafe exactly when q(m−1)/(q+m−1) < R < qm/(q+m), an interval of exact width q^2/((q+m)(q+m−1)). For one intervening skip this specializes to the two-thirds band (q(2q+1)/(3q+1), 2q(q+1)/(3q+2)), whose width is below 1/9; integral reciprocals never lie there, and the corresponding positive odd numerator is at least 7. These are local constraints: no theorem here says that the actual greedy orbit for 1/2 avoids a band or identifies the surviving last-producer cells with unsafe skips.
assertions.status_meaning: Lean theorem in the committed formal-source checkpoint; no novelty assertion is implied

assertions.label: Campbell shift-synchronization strategy boundary
assertions.statement: Campbell's application of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate chooses delta = 1/4, so at prime-search height X the progression modulus d must satisfy d <= X^(1/4), equivalently d^4 <= X. In the proposed last-skip synchronization, P is the fatal-window prime cap, t the unavoidable phase period, and d the combined progression modulus. Taking X = P, the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, and d^4 <= P are inconsistent. The shifted-zero interface is guarded by a putative last skip and is exactly equivalent to infinitely many actual greedy skips and to membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. It is an endpoint restatement, not an independent Campbell input, and proves no half-membership.

assertions.label: Complex first-harmonic pivot decomposition
assertions.statement: For each positive cofactor m at most sqrt(X)/2, the canonical supplier fibre is exactly the injective image of the primes p in the shifted product interval under N = mp - (L-s+1). This exact bijection does not make a supplier prime globally isolated: at X=16, L=20, s=1, m=2, N=18 the pivot is 38=2*19, while the same prime 19 divides the distinct window argument N+1=19. Removing the pivot phase gives an exact decomposition of the block first-harmonic sum into a centred supplier-fibre correlation, a supplier-fibre mean term, a bad-supplier term, and a non-supplier term. At a positive scale satisfying the explicit dyadic-room inequality, if the real part of the centred term is at most 14X/25 and the other three norms are at most X/100, X/100, and 8X/25, then the real first-harmonic sum is at most 9X/10 and yields a finite certificate. A cofinal supply of these budgets implies irrationality of S. No global supplier-prime isolation, prime-distribution estimate, or decorrelation estimate supplying the budgets is proved.

declarations.docstring: **All-rank shift-algebra no-go.** For every `t ≥ 3`, one nonzero synthetic pulse simultaneously compensates every finite integer shift polynomial. \item\label{res:factorideal} \stag{unconditional progress}
\textbf{LCM factor-ideal shift-algebra no-go.}  For every $t\ge3$, with
$H=\lcm(1,\ldots,t)$, there is a nonzero synthetic dyadic coboundary whose
forcing letters reproduce the actual totient differences at $t-2$ prescribed
indices and lie in the ideal generated by $\varphi(H)$.  Every finite integer
shift polynomial preserves the exact coboundary cancellation, the $H$-factor
ideal and all lower factor ideals, together with uniform state and letter
bounds.  A sparse-anchor variant also preserves every prescribed whole-ray
anchor.  Hence factor ideals, finite shift-algebra closure and these bounds
cannot by themselves force a contradiction.  The witness is synthetic: its
letters are not claimed to be actual totient differences, nonlinear
combinations are outside the theorem, and no cofinal family of certificates
follows.
{\footnotesize\emph{Checked:}
\mword{Erdos249257/LcmFactorIdealPulseObstruction.lean}{798}{lcm_factorIdeal_finiteRank_shiftAlgebra_not_sufficient}{finite shift-algebra no-go}.}

assertions.statement: For a ≥ 8 and J + (a + 6) < 2·2^a, the true translated LCM-orbit difference is strictly positive. If it is represented by an integer and the dyadic modulus has room for the directed endpoint strip, the carry survivor is strictly negative and the discrepancy residue is exactly the top-edge representative 2^K − carry_K, strictly between the strip’s lower edge and 2^K. declarations.name: actualLcmTailDiff_shift_pos
declarations.signature: theorem actualLcmTailDiff_shift_pos {a J : ℕ} (ha : 8 ≤ a) (hshort : J + (a + 6) < 2 * 2 ^ a) : 0 < totientTail (2 * periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) - totientTail (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J)
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional positive-sign corridor.** At a power-of-two LCM height, the true translated tail difference stays positive as long as an `a+6`-term lookahead remains inside the short arithmetic window. The first lookahead letter already contributes more than enough: its quarter-height lower bound, amplified by `2^(a+5) = 32 * 2^a`, dominates four copies of the LCM height. All remaining lookahead letters are positive, and the directed lower bound controls the untranslated infinite remainder.

declarations.signature: theorem actualLcm_trueEndpointSurvivor_neg {a J K : ℕ} (ha : 8 ≤ a) (hshort : J + K + (a + 6) < 2 * 2 ^ a) {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (2 * periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) - totientTail (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J)) : -carryOrbit (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) d K < 0 ∧ endpointSurvivor (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) K (-carryOrbit (periodLcm (2 ^ a)) (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) d K)
declarations.docstring: **Survivor-sign consumer.** If a translated actual LCM orbit is integral at the start of the positive corridor, then at every later endpoint which still has an `a+6`-letter lookahead, the survivor supplied by the true carry is strictly negative. Thus the nonnegative true-survivor branch is eliminated; this does not assert that the finite survivor set has no nonnegative spurious elements.

declarations.name: actualLcm_integral_forces_topEdgeResidue
declarations.signature: theorem actualLcm_integral_forces_topEdgeResidue {a J K : ℕ} (ha : 8 ≤ a) (hshort : J + K + (a + 6) < 2 * 2 ^ a) {d : ℤ} (hd : (d : ℝ) = totientTail (2 * periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J) - totientTail (periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J)) (hroom : ((2 * periodLcm (2 ^ a) + J + K + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) < (2 : ℤ) ^ K) : let H
declarations.docstring: **Exact obstruction to a sign-only modular kill.** Once the dyadic modulus is wider than the directed endpoint strip, integrality together with the positive-sign corridor does not put the discrepancy residue in the central arc. It forces the opposite: the residue is exactly the top-edge representative `2^K - carry_K`. Consequently the upper inequality required by `directedCertifiedKill` fails strictly. Any contradiction after the sign theorem therefore needs an independent arithmetic exclusion of this top boundary band; the carry reset alone merely re-encodes the persistent negative survivor.

assertions.statement: A uniform 11/100 nonpositive-phase density on arbitrarily late dyadic blocks yields an 89/100 first-harmonic saving and hence a finite certificate; alternatively, cofinally many natural prime indices with tail-orbit real part below 9/10 yield adaptive pivot escape. The exact initial phase is the scaled-angle character of (2^h - 1) times the series, and the tail phase follows a power-of-two squaring orbit from it; phase 1 is equivalent to an integral actual tail difference, while an entered dyadic root obstructs the strict-gap producer.

\begin{theorem}[terminal scaled vanishing implies the half-value]
\label{res:terminalhalf}
Let $S$ be a
\texttt{HalfTerminalOnlyScaledVanishingSequence}: its finite words exclude
ranks $0$ and $1$, their depths tend to infinity, and the absolute terminal
carry divided by $2^M$ tends to zero along the depths $M$.  Then there is an
infinite set $A\subseteq\N$ with

\[
  \sum_{a\in A}\frac1{2^a-1}=\frac12.
\]
Consequently the universal irrationality assertion in
Problem~\ref{res:problem} is false under this hypothesis.  This is a
conditional implication, not a construction of $S$ and not a solution
of Problem~\#257.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[cofinal cylinders imply an infinite half-support]
\label{res:cylinderhalf}
Suppose that for every $N$ there are $M,K$ with
$\max\{N,1\}\le M$ and a nonempty

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[finite-period noncollapse]\label{res:period}
Let $F\subseteq\Npos$ be finite and nonempty, let $b\ge2$ be an integer, and
let $D_F>0$ be the denominator of $x_F(b)$ in lowest terms.  Then $D_F$ is
coprime to $b$, and
\[
  \operatorname{ord}_{D_F}(b)=\lcm\{n:n\in F\}.
\]
If moreover $\lcm(F)\ge2$, then $\lcm(F)<D_F$.
\end{theorem}

paper_anchor.section_title: An integral basis for factorial channels

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[divisor-channel coordinates]\label{res:divisor-channel-coordinates}
Set
\[
T_n=ne_{n-1}-e_n,\qquad
U_n=T_n-\sum_{\substack{d\mid n\\2\le d<n}}W_{d,n}U_d
\quad(n\ge2).
\]
Then
\[
M(U_n)=0,\qquad V_d(U_n)=(d!-1)\mathbf1_{d=n}.
\]
The vectors $e_1,U_2,U_3,\ldots$ form an integral basis.  Every finite vector
has the unique finite expansion
\begin{equation}
\lambda=M(\lambda)e_1+
\sum_{d\ge2}\frac{V_d(\lambda)-M(\lambda)}{d!-1}U_d.
\label{eq:channel-basis-expansion}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{problem}[Erd\H{o}s \#243]\label{res:problem}
Let $1\le a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be a sequence of integers with
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^{2}}=1
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \sum\frac{1}{a_n}\in\Q .
\]
Then $a_n=a_{n-1}^{2}-a_{n-1}+1$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
\end{problem}

\begin{theorem}[finite negative relative mass]\label{res:massscalar}\label{res:mass}
Let $C_n$ be positive integers and $E_n$ integers satisfying
$C_{n+1}=C_n-E_n$. If
\[
 \sum_n\frac{(-E_n)_+}{C_n}<\infty,
\]
then $E_n=0$ eventually. No denominator dynamics or normalised vanishing
is required.
\end{theorem}

\]

is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[sparse congruence-preserving rationalisation]\label{res:sparserationalisation}
Let $a_n$ be nonnegative integers with $\sum_{n\ge0}a_n2^{-(n+1)}=A<\infty$,
let $K\in\N$, and let $f:\N\to\R$ tend to $+\infty$.  There exist a set
$S\subseteq[K,\infty)$ of upper Banach density zero and a nondegenerate
interval $I\subset(A,\infty)$ such that every $r\in I$ is realised by a
nonnegative correction $e$ supported on $S$, with $0\le e_n\le f(n)$
eventually, $\sum(a_n+e_n)2^{-(n+1)}=r$, and every fixed modulus eventually
dividing both $e_n$ and $\sum_{i<n}e_i$.  For the actual prime gaps and
every $0<\varepsilon<1$ the same construction may be taken with
$e_n\le(\log(n+3))^\varepsilon$ eventually and
$|S\cap[X,2X)|=O_\varepsilon(X/\log\log X)$, so that all unnormalised blocks
of length $o(\log\log X)$ are preserved in total variation.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[affine and fixed-lattice circularity]\label{res:affinecollapse}
For every rational dyadic tail recurrence and all $h,N,r\ge0$,
\[
 \mathcal A_{N,r}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D_N\in2\Z.
\tag{2.1}\label{eq:affinecollapse}
\]
Consequently, if every $\delta_N$ is even, then
\[
 \bigl(\forall N_0\ \exists N,r:\ N_0<N\text{ and }\neg\mathcal A_{N,r}\bigr)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D_N\notin\Z\text{ for arbitrarily large }N.
\tag{2.2}\label{eq:affinecofinal}
\]

There is a second equivalence.  Let $b:\N\to\Q$ satisfy
$|D_N|\le b(N)$ for every $N$, and suppose that for every $N$ and every
positive integer $q$ there is an $r$ with
\[
 2b(N+r)q<2^r.
\tag{2.3}\label{eq:dyadicscale}
\]
Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\forall N_0\ \exists N,r:\ N_0<N\text{ and }
   \forall z\in\Z,\quad
   b(N+r)<|B_{h,N,r}-2^rz|\\
 &\hspace{35mm}\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D_N\notin\Z\text{ for arbitrarily large }N.
 \end{split}
\tag{2.4}\label{eq:fixedcollapse}
\]
\end{theorem}

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[adjacent small-shift obstruction]\label{res:smallpair}
Let $T:\N\to\Q$ satisfy the dyadic tail recurrence with integer digits $g$.
Fix $h$ and $N$.  If
\[
 -1<\sigma_h(N)<1,\qquad -1<\sigma_h(N+1)<1,
 \qquad g_{N+h+1}\ne g_{N+1},
\]
then $\sigma_h(N)$ and $\sigma_h(N+1)$ cannot both be integral.
Consequently, if such a pair occurs beyond every threshold, the $h$-shift is
not eventually integral.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[arbitrary-order non-separability]\label{res:infinite-rank}
Let $p,q,r$ be primes with $p\ne q$, $p\ne r$ and $q\ne r$.  For every
$n\ge0$ there are injective maps $I,J:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\N$ such that, for
every $k\ge0$,
\[
 \det\bigl(\Kernel(I(a),J(b),k)\bigr)_{0\le a,b<n}\ne0.
\]
Consequently, for no finite $d$ do there exist rational-valued functions
$f_\ell(i)$ and $G_\ell(j,k)$, $0\le\ell<d$, satisfying
\[
 \Kernel(i,j,k)=\sum_{\ell<d}f_\ell(i)G_\ell(j,k)
 \qquad\hbox{for all }i,j,k.
\]
\end{theorem}

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[critical-value separation]\label{res:critical-value-separation}
Let $f$ be monic of degree $n$, let $c$ be a simple critical point with
$v=f(c)\ne0$, and let $S>1$.  Suppose every other critical point $d$ of $f$
satisfies
\[
  \Bigl|1-\frac{f(d)}{v}\Bigr|\ge S .
\]
Then the square-root-resolved inverse branch through $c$ joins two roots of
$f$ inside $\{|f|\le|v|\}$ by a path of length at most
\[
  2\,|v|^{1/n}(1+S)^{1/n}\sqrt{\log\frac{S}{S-1}} .
\]
In particular the connector is shorter than $2|v|^{1/n}$ whenever
\begin{equation}\label{eq:separation-threshold}
  (1+S)^{2/n}\log\frac{S}{S-1}<1 .
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[disk-family uniform radius]\label{res:critical-value-thresholds}
A strictly stronger disk-family theorem, proved in
\href{https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/f36a98bf3d3e6f65f1074e3b800e3293d5b8a51a/ErdosProblems/Erdos1041/DiskFamilyCriticalValueSeparation.md}{disk family critical value separation}, replaces

 \le\frac4\pi\operatorname{artanh}(q^2)\,\|h\|_{A^2}^2
\]
and yields a uniform radius $S=4/3$ in every degree $n\ge3$, at every real
centre.  The smallest degree-uniform radius certified by that coefficient at
centre $a\in[0,1]$ is
$S_\infty(a)=(A+\sqrt{A^2-4a(1-a)})/2$ with $A=\coth 1$; the endpoints recover $S_\infty(0)=S_\infty(1)=\coth1$ already on file.
An obstructing critical value may depend on the proposed centre.  The older
coefficientwise regimes $S=4$ ($n\ge3$), $S=3$ ($n\ge4$), and $S=2$ ($n\ge6$)
remain valid and are superseded.  A proposed all-degree cutoff $S=3/2$ for
the older bound is strictly weaker than $4/3$ and is not used.
\end{corollary}

\label{res:sharp-collinear-root-diameter}
Let $f$ be monic of degree $n\ge2$, with collinear zero occurrences of diameter

scaled Chebyshev root configuration with extreme roots at distance $D$.

\begin{theorem}[weighted free-point inequality in every degree]
\label{res:fp-weighted-all-degree}
Let $c_1,\ldots,c_m\in\overline{\mathbb D}$ and let $w_j>0$ satisfy

 \sum_j w_j G(c_j)^2\le 1,
\]

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[exact attachment-age/lifetime currency]
\label{res:orlicz-currency}
Define
\[
 \Phi(x)=\int_0^x\frac{dt}{\log(\coth t)}\qquad(x\ge0).
\]
At $t=0$ the integrand is understood by its continuous limiting value $0$
(equivalently, the integral is improper at that endpoint).
For every integer $k\ge1$ and $0<r\le1$, with
$x=k^{-1}\log(1/r)$,
\[
 I_k(r)=k\Phi(x).                                      \tag{O1}
\]
The function $\Phi$ is increasing and strictly convex on $(0,\infty)$, and
\[
 \frac{\Phi(x)}x\longrightarrow0\qquad(x\downarrow0). \tag{O2}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $k\ge1$ and every $c>0$, some $0<r<1$
satisfies
\[
 I_k(r)<c\,\frac1k\log\frac1r.                        \tag{O3}
\]
In particular, there is no positive universal linear conversion from
attachment age to lifetime.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[capacity-defect closure]
\label{res:constant-factor-capacity}
Keep the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{res:constant-factor-arity} with

\[

 A=\frac{283}{3610},\qquad B=\frac{52029}{9100},
\]

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[critical-value separation]
\label{res:critical-value-separation}
Let $P$ be a polynomial of degree $n\ge3$ whose leading coefficient has
modulus one.  Suppose
\[
 P(0)=1,\qquad P'(0)=0,\qquad P''(0)\ne0,
\]
and, for some $S>1$, every other critical point $d\ne0$ satisfies
\[
 |1-P(d)|\ge S.
\]
If $Z$ is either local solution at the saddle of
\[
 P(Z(\xi))=1-\xi^2,\qquad Z(0)=0,
\]
then $Z$ continues holomorphically and injectively to
$|\xi|<\sqrt S$.  Its endpoints $Z(-1)$ and $Z(1)$ are distinct roots, the
curve $Z([-1,1])$ lies in $\{|P|\le1\}$, and their resolved inverse-ray
connector satisfies
\[
 \int_{-1}^{1}|Z'(\xi)|\,d\xi
 \le 2\Bigl(\frac2n\Bigr)^{1/(2n)}S^{1/n}
     \sqrt{\log\!\frac{S}{S-1}}.       \tag{4}
\]
In particular the connector has length strictly below $2$ whenever
\[
 \Bigl(\frac{2S^{2}}{n}\Bigr)^{1/n}\log\!\frac{S}{S-1}<1. \tag{5}
\]
\end{theorem}

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[critical-value budget in every degree]
\label{res:critical-value-budget}
Let $f$ be monic of degree $n\ge2$, with roots in a closed disc of radius
$R\ge0$.  If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points counted with
multiplicity, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-value-power-budget}
 \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|f(c_j)|^{1/(n-1)}\le(n-1)R^{n/(n-1)}.
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|f(c_j)|^{1/n}\le(n-1)R.
\]
The constant is attained by $f(z)=(z-\tau)^n-\lambda$ with enclosing
disk centred at $\tau$ and radius $R=|\lambda|^{1/n}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Archimedean cap on base-uniform rank-two families]
\label{res:archimedean-cap}
Let $(U_n,V_n)$ be pairs in $\mathbb Z[X]^2$ satisfying $\Lambda_n(x)=U_n(x)F(x)-V_n(x)\ne0$,
$\deg U_n,\deg V_n\le\delta n^2(1+o(1))$,
$\log\max(H(U_n),H(V_n))\le h n^2(1+o(1))$ with $H$ the $\ell^1$ coefficient
norm, and
$\log|\Lambda_n(x)|=-\sigma n^2\log x\,(1+o(1))$ for every real $x>1$, with
$\sigma,\delta>0$ and $h\ge0$ independent of $x$.  Then with
$d_n=\max(\deg U_n,\deg V_n)$, the homogenised forms
$b^{d_n}\Lambda_n(a/b)$ tend to zero whenever
$\log b/\log a<\sigma/(\sigma+\delta)$, and $\sigma/(\sigma+\delta)\le1/2$.
\end{theorem}

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[binary four-jet collision]\label{res:jetkernel}
Fix a width \(W\) and depths \(R,S\), and let \((U_j,V_j)_{j<M}\) be any \(M\)
pairs of integral polynomials.  Call a subset of \(\{0,\dots,M-1\}\), equivalently
a vector of \(\{0,1\}^M\), a \emph{binary selector}.  If the
\(2^M\) binary selectors outnumber the finite four-jet target
\[
 (\Z/3^R\Z)^2\times(\Z/2^S\Z)^2,
\]
then two distinct subsets have the same four-jet sum.  Subtracting their
indicator vectors gives a nonzero coefficient vector in
\(\{-1,0,1\}^M\) cancelling all four jets.  The target has exact cardinality
\[
 (3^R)^2(2^S)^2.
\]
In particular, if \(R>0\) and \(4R+2S\le M\), such a collision exists.
\end{theorem}

source_excerpt.text:
\begin{theorem}[B\'ezout--Pl\"ucker tail collapse]
\label{res:plucker-collapse}
Let $R_0$ be a commutative ring and let $w_n=(A_n,B_n)\in R_0^2$.  Suppose
that every row is unimodular ($u_n A_n+v_n B_n=1$ for some $u_n,v_n$) and every adjacent minor vanishes:
\[
 A_nB_{n+1}-B_nA_{n+1}=0\qquad(n\ge0).
\]
Then every pairwise minor $A_iB_j-B_iA_j$ vanishes.  In particular, take
$R_0=\Z/(2^S3^R)\Z$ with $R>0$.  If $S+2R\le k$, there are two distinct
binary selectors $s,t\in\{0,1\}^{k}$ such that
\[
 \sum_{i<k}s_iw_i=\sum_{i<k}t_iw_i.
\]
Thus the sufficient width is $S+2R$, rather than the ambient two-coordinate
width $2S+4R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[quantitative bounded-fibre escape]\label{res:boundedfibre}
Let $A,B,J$ be finite sets and let $f:A\to B$, $g:A\to\mathbb R$ and
$\iota:A\to J$.  Suppose that each simultaneous fibre of $(f,g)$ has at
most $k$ elements and that, for some $\delta>0$,
\[
 \iota(x)=\iota(y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad |g(x)-g(y)|<\delta.
\]
If $|B||J|k<|A|$, then some distinct $x,y\in A$ satisfy
\[
 f(x)=f(y),\qquad 0<|g(x)-g(y)|<\delta.
\]
\end{theorem}

claim_fidelity.why_this_exists: Every other gate checks that a citation lands. This one checks that the sentence at the near end of the link says what the theorem at the far end proves. The founding case: a claim said a bound held 'uniformly in the support' while the declaration it cited bound the support before the existential, and the declaration's own docstring said outright that it exports no such uniform constant. Coordinates all resolved. The mathematics did not agree.
claim_fidelity.authority_order: checked Lean source is proof authority; the manuscript owns exposition; the registry sentence is a projection of both. When they disagree the projection is what is wrong.
claim_fidelity.mechanical_only: Findings are produced by parsing binder order, dependency subscripts, denial sentences and status tags. Differences that need a mathematician are reported as 'not_mechanically_decidable' rather than decided here.
claim_fidelity.disclosure_rule: A claim carrying a finding must also carry the finding on its own row. The build stops otherwise. The correction lives upstream in the published claims registry, so this packet cannot fix the sentence -- it can only guarantee no reader meets it alone.

verdict_legend.overstrong: a surface the claim cites contradicts its own sentence. Upstream correction required; carried in upstream_defects.
verdict_legend.not_mechanically_decidable: the surfaces differ in a way this check cannot adjudicate. Recorded on the row so nobody relies on the sentence unexamined, and not asserted as an error.

paper_results.why_this_exists: The row layer was built from the Lean claims registry and the per-problem index, so it indexed what is formalised rather than what is proved. A paper-only theorem had nowhere to be a row. The #269 two-prime transcendence theorems -- unconditional, complete, and the strongest finished mathematics in the corpus -- were invisible to every query route while the headline said they were recorded in their problem row.
paper_results.selection_rule: Every label the manuscripts prefix 'res:', which is the authors' own marker for a result, tagged with the environment they wrote it in. This build ranks nothing and omits nothing it can read; the selection was made in the manuscript.
paper_results.what_a_row_here_means: This statement is proved in this manuscript at this line. It does not mean a Lean declaration covers it, and it does not mean the claims registry reviewed it.

row_shape.statement: the title the author gave the environment, which names the result rather than stating it. The proved statement is the LaTeX in paper_anchor.source_excerpt.text -- quoted exactly, so it reads without a network
row_shape.evidence_authority: 'manuscript_argument' on every row here: proved in the manuscript by a written argument. Whether a Lean declaration also covers it is not determined by this index, and is not implied
row_shape.reviewed: false on every row here. The claims registry carries reviewed claims for #249 and #257 only, so a manuscript result outside it is authored mathematics that no registry entry reviews. This is a statement about the registry's scope, not about the mathematics
row_shape.problem_ids: the manuscript's subject, read from the paper id. The joint #249/#257 gateway is bound to neither, because binding it to one would be a false narrowing
row_shape.paper_status_tag: present only where the author wrote a \stag marker; one manuscript uses them
row_shape.lean_coverage: lean_coverage_status is present on every paper-only row. A manuscript status tag can establish declared formalisation; otherwise not_declared_for_this_result is an explicit unknown, not a claim that no Lean theorem bears on the result. A source-authored per-result manifest is the upgrade contract.

paper_results.coverage_before: the paper anchor index scanned only manuscripts a registered claim cited: 3 of 13

lean_coverage_manifest.upgrade_contract: Publish a source-authored per-result manifest mapping paper id and result label to checked Lean declaration ids. Until then, absence of a manuscript status tag stays explicitly unknown.

source_lane_legend.what_this_is: the body of source a row's authority comes from, on every row. It is derived from assertion_kind, which maps one-to-one onto it -- so it adds no evidence, and agreement between the two fields corroborates nothing. It is here so that any sentence about where rows come from can be generated from the axis it is about, instead of from 'reviewed', which answers a different question.
source_lane_legend.registry_claim: docs/claims.json -- a curated claim the release reviews and publishes with a status. reviewed=true

source_lane_legend.why_two_unreviewed_lanes_matter: reviewed=false now covers both a kernel-checked Lean declaration and a paper argument with no formalisation asserted. Collapsing them loses the difference between 'the machine checked it, the registry did not review it' and 'a person proved it in prose'.

lane_binding.why_this_exists: The manuscript rows were appended to a collection that four finished surfaces already described, and each kept describing the collection it was written against. The published count said 256 while the array held 347; the single-row contract promised two fields ninety-one rows did not carry; every per-problem frontier said an empty result meant the evidence was in the expansion lane, including for the problem whose strongest finished theorem had just been indexed. None of it raised: an empty list is a valid answer and a stale integer is still an integer.
lane_binding.label_only_meaning: the manuscript gave the environment no title, so the row's statement field falls back to the label. statement_grain says so on the row; quote paper_anchor.source_excerpt.text instead.
lane_binding.standing_rule: A new assertion kind is not landed until the count, the row contract, the per-problem frontier, the lane map, the recap and the route tests have all been told it exists. plectis_query_contracts sweeps the whole return domain of every route for exactly this reason.

canonical_gateway.thesis: Archival joint #249/#257 manuscript. Current mathematical entrances are the eight short problem notes.

retained_companions.thesis: Complete working record for Erdős #249: checked premises, finite certificates, closed routes, evidence bands, and surviving obligations.
Complete working record for Erdős #257: Lean full-support and structured-support theorems, finite-support geometry, and surviving arbitrary-infinite-support obligations.

Complete working record for Erdős #1041: Lean Newton-flow decay, ray separation, translation geometry, Comparator-checked solved-family kernels, ordinary path assemblies, and the unresolved global topology and metric gluing.

Complete reasoning record for Erdős #1049. Ordinary F(31/4) and region theorems citing Zudilin; Lean supporting arithmetic, not those irrationality theorems; outstanding 3/2 approximant. The problem remains open.
Complete reasoning record for Erdős #68. Lean Core carry equivalences are distinct from ordinary LCM-liminf and finite prime-cancellation examples. The problem remains open.

Complete reasoning record for Erdős #243. Lean integer-state rigidity, including a scalar finite-negative-mass criterion; cubic-rate and Chebotarev steps are ordinary. Mixed-sign unbounded regime remains open.

Complete reasoning record for Erdős #251. Countermodel and finite counting reduction; the prime-to-gap identity is already-known and does not use the prime-number theorem. The actual-prime tail witness remains open.
Complete reasoning record for Erdős #269. Two-prime credit is Steve Fan's; three-prime Lean rank/window versus unproved cofinal escape. The problem remains open.

problem_series.thesis: The Core carry equivalences (FactorialGapPlateauCore isolation pin; FactorialZeroPlateau is the default-root duplicate), two incomparable finite denominator exclusions (GMP m = 300000 and continued-fraction q ≥ 2^39990), and the still-open cofinal-carry producer.

The integer-state bounded-negative theorem under explicit centring, bounded-negative, and normalised-vanishing hypotheses (Lean); the original-coordinate corollary is an ordinary transfer. Mixed-sign unbounded negative mass remains open.

Exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e ≥ 1 (Lean), infinite-dimensionality equivalent to Coons for integer-valued sequence modules, all-base exact rank using Martin externally, finite Farey exclusion and t ≤ 82 certificates, and no infinite witness.

A coefficient-only countermodel and sparse rationalising perturbation as the supported lead; the already-known prime-to-gap identity checked without the prime-number theorem; cofinal small-mismatch tail witness open.

Lean full-support irrationality and Lean structured supports (pairwise-coprime plus summable; eventually-periodic); ordinary reciprocal-summable theorem without coprimality; arbitrary infinite support and the 1/2 and 1/21 branches remain open and distinct.

Three-prime Lean rank/window structure; Steve Fan's two-prime transcendence (26 June 2026) recorded as ordinary plus Bugeaud–Laurent, with no Lean theorem or priority claim; cofinal local-window escape remains open.
Lean Newton-flow/ray/root-retention and Comparator-checked solved-family kernels; ordinary all-degree trinomial, 13/25, Poisson, and length-<2 assemblies; global topology remains open.

Ordinary Zudilin specialization that F(31/4) and its positive powers are irrational; Lean supporting height-region, 3/2 corridor, tail recurrence, and selected Hankel identities; outstanding 3/2 approximant with remainder control.

publication_architecture.problem_series_boundary: A problem note expounds declarations of the ErdosProblems expansion root. Those declarations are exact Lean propositions and are not reviewed public claims; no note may be read as promoting one, and no Erdős problem it treats is closed.

retirement_notices.thesis: The former one-sided Erdős Problem 249 specialist note is not an active mathematical paper; its archived predecessor is historical evidence only, and the registered Lean claims remain queryable from the claim registry.

architecture_guides.thesis: A first-principles map of the Lean source, reviewed public claims, authored documents, generated views, release commands, GitHub workflow, and the exact boundary between human judgement and automatic checks.

agent_native_guides.thesis: A cold-clone-to-proof-receipt architecture: exhaustive and selective navigation layers, bounded intent routing, a session notary whose verdicts come from Lean, focused changed-cone builds, exact dependency-index cache receipts, one replayed dogfood session, and explicit transfer limits.

edge_semantics.corollary_of: The source claim is presented as a corollary or specialization of the target claim.
edge_semantics.builds_on: The source claim's argument layer builds on the target claim or criterion.
edge_semantics.eliminates_case: The source claim eliminates a named branch or cell in the target reduction without discharging its remaining residual.
edge_semantics.makes_exact: The source claim records why a reduction or certificate formulation loses no information.

The exact residue classifier excludes a bounded positive carry state whose canonical least-positive representative exceeds the bound. It constrains the reduced tail without excluding the integral branch, which is what pointwise nonintegrality of every reduced tail would do.

The checked consumer takes the denominator-dependent cofinal local-window residue escape as its hypothesis, so this proposition is exactly the input that would discharge it for every multiplier coprime to 30.

The finite-observer formalisation isolates the faithfulness requirement a two-dimensional representation must meet, and shows that a genuine finite-dimensional factorisation forces a finite realised span. It supplies no representation and excludes none.

The bounded-rise barrier is a state-level obstruction on the canonical orbit and is one of the inputs the overlap-height growth question would feed. It proves no lower bound on the growth of the overlap height.

Membership of 1/21 is proved equivalent to cofinally bounded scaled actual greedy remainders, so this proposition is that criterion stated as the remaining obligation.
The exact six-step defect recurrence and the slope-aware repair-load equivalence say which quantities a bounded-memory invariant would have to track. No invariant is constructed and none is excluded.

On the complementary fatal branch the last-skip approximant is pinned inside an exact one-sided interval around the Erdos-Borwein constant. Turning that interval into a contradiction still needs the final-skip signatures this proposition asks for.

prime_gap_unboundedness.source_statement: The gaps between consecutive primes are unbounded; the elementary factorial construction gives arbitrarily long prime-free intervals.
prime_gap_unboundedness.mapping: The local theorem uses the zero-based consecutive-prime gap sequence and proves that for every bound B some indexed gap exceeds B. This is the same unboundedness statement after the repository's indexing convention is unfolded.
prime_gap_unboundedness.historical_attribution: Classical elementary factorial prime-free interval argument; modern large-gap theorems in the paper are contextual and strictly stronger.
prime_gap_unboundedness.logical_dependency: The Lean proof reconstructs an elementary argument locally; no external prime-gap theorem is imported as a proof dependency.

eventually_periodic_lambert.source_statement: For an eventually periodic sequence of nonnegative rational coefficients that is not eventually zero, the associated Lambert series at an integer base b at least 2 is irrational.
eventually_periodic_lambert.mapping: The local theorem formalises the nonnegative rational eventually-periodic coefficient case. Its coefficient, base, sign, and non-eventual-zero hypotheses are kept explicit; it does not claim the broader mixed-sign theorem.
eventually_periodic_lambert.historical_attribution: Luca and Tachiya, Irrationality of Lambert series associated with a periodic sequence (2014), with the later RIMS exposition used for statement comparison.
eventually_periodic_lambert.logical_dependency: The local Lean proof uses a separate periodic-divisor certificate route; the cited paper establishes attribution and source fidelity, not a kernel dependency.

known_irrational_supports.source_statement: Several structured support families for the Mersenne reciprocal subseries are known to give irrational sums, including full support and other classical or later special families.
known_irrational_supports.mapping: The review family is an aggregate disclosure. Each local theorem retains its own support predicate; the Comparator selects full support as the classical representative and pairwise-coprime support as a dedicated exact non-dilation representative.
known_irrational_supports.historical_attribution: Erdos (1948) for full support; Erdos (1968), Luca--Tachiya, and Tao--Teravainen for the specific additional families identified in the paper and prior-art ledger.
known_irrational_supports.logical_dependency: The full-support and pairwise-coprime Comparator theorems are proved locally in Lean. Other family rows have their stated local or cited proof boundaries; historical attribution is not an imported Lean dependency.

pairwise_coprime_support.source_statement: For every integer base b at least 2 and every infinite pairwise-coprime support A with summable reciprocal mass, the support-restricted Mersenne reciprocal series is irrational.
pairwise_coprime_support.mapping: The local theorem keeps the base, infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses explicit and concludes irrationality of erdosSupportSeries b A. At base 2 this is exactly the pairwise-coprime support subfamily of Erdős #257; it is a separate non-dilation representative from the full-support row.
pairwise_coprime_support.historical_attribution: Erdos (1968), as recorded in the repository's prior-art ledger and the #257 problem note.
pairwise_coprime_support.logical_dependency: The proof-bearing source supplies the adaptive CRT and weighted coefficient certificate argument locally; the cited source establishes historical attribution and statement fidelity, not an imported Lean dependency.

achievement_set_geometry.source_statement: Kakeya's strict-tail criterion places rapidly decreasing subsum sets in the Cantor-set regime; for the fixed-base Mersenne sequence, Kovač--Tao verify the strict-tail inequality and distinct subsums.
achievement_set_geometry.mapping: At base 2 the local development formalises compactness, perfection, total disconnectedness, nowhere density, and measure one. The strict-tail Cantor geometry aligns with the cited antecedents; the measure-one clause is locally derived and carries no novelty assertion.
achievement_set_geometry.historical_attribution: Kakeya (1914) for the strict-tail subsum-set criterion and Kovač--Tao (2025), Remark 4.1, for the fixed-base Mersenne antecedent.
achievement_set_geometry.logical_dependency: The topology and measure theorem are proved locally in Lean; the cited sources fix historical/source alignment and are not imported proof objects.

erdos_borwein_full_support.source_statement: For every integer b at least 2, the full-support Lambert--Mersenne series sum over n at least 1 of 1/(b^n-1) is irrational.
erdos_borwein_full_support.mapping: The local theorem uses Nat indexing with exponent k+1, which is exactly the source sum after reindexing n=k+1; the base assumption is the same integer condition b at least 2.
erdos_borwein_full_support.historical_attribution: Erdos, On arithmetical properties of Lambert series (1948), theorem on p. 63 as recorded in the repository's prior-art ledger.
erdos_borwein_full_support.logical_dependency: The theorem is independently represented and proved in Lean in this repository; the historical source is attribution and fidelity evidence, not an imported kernel dependency.

totient_kernel_rank.source_statement: Coons proved that Euler's totient sequence is not k-regular for every integer k at least 2, while Martin's affine-totient ordering theorem implies linear independence of every finite family of pairwise nonproportional positive-slope affine totient sections.
totient_kernel_rank.mapping: The dyadic Lean development gives an independent constructive finite-level basis and rank proof. Its full-kernel infinite-dimensionality corollary is kernel-checked here but is not an independent contribution: for integer-valued sequence modules it is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity result. The all-base Lean modules check the zero-channel identity, the exact composite-base scalar reduction, residue coordinates, index cardinality k^e+1, and unconditional spanning by the canonical family. Lean also checks the exact-rank conclusion under an explicit linear-independence hypothesis. Martin remains the external authority for that hypothesis, so the unconditional all-base basis and rank theorem remains a paper conclusion rather than a Lean theorem without assumptions.
totient_kernel_rank.historical_attribution: Coons for non-k-regularity of Euler's totient sequence; Martin for the positive-density affine ordering theorem from which the paper's finite-family independence step follows.
totient_kernel_rank.logical_dependency: The dyadic finite-level proof is local. In the all-base development, arithmetic reduction and canonical spanning are unconditional; exact rank is conditional on an explicit linear-independence hypothesis. The paper discharges that hypothesis using Martin externally, whose positive-density theorem is not formalised.

prime_gap_irrationality_equivalence.source_statement: The prime-value dyadic series equals 2 plus the prime-gap dyadic series by summation by parts, so one series is irrational exactly when the other is.
prime_gap_irrationality_equivalence.mapping: The local named iff still takes a Summable hypothesis. This checkout discharges that hypothesis by the elementary polynomial bound p_n ≤ 1250(n+1)^4 and the unconditional identity, not by the prime-number theorem. Neither side is proved irrational.
prime_gap_irrationality_equivalence.historical_attribution: Tao, erdosproblems.com/251, 7 October 2025. Recorded as cited only on prime_gap_identity_tao. This is not a novelty or priority claim.
prime_gap_irrationality_equivalence.logical_dependency: The Lean proof reconstructs summation by parts and an elementary prime bound locally; the forum post is attribution, not a kernel import.

main_results.statement: Irrationality is equivalent to cofinally many strict-successor divisibility failures.
main_results.boundary: The equivalence does not prove that the cofinal failures occur.

main_results.statement: Irrationality is equivalent to cofinally many non-unit carries.
main_results.boundary: The equivalence does not supply a cofinal carry producer.

main_results.statement: Normalised vanishing and bounded rise exclude a cofinally bounded negative part.
main_results.boundary: All dynamics, bounded-rise, positivity, and vanishing hypotheses remain explicit.

main_results.contribution_class: locally proved signed recovery/rigidity theorem; novelty unassessed
main_results.statement: Under exact natural C/D dynamics with a > 1, C > 0, E = D - (a - 1)C, strict |E| < C, a uniform lower bound on E, and division-free normalized vanishing, boundedNegativePart_eventually_zero forces E = 0 eventually; centered-zero plus an eventually nonzero next tail recovers eventual Sylvester recurrence.
main_results.boundary: The signed theorem has a C D : ℕ → ℕ, E : ℕ → ℤ, and B : ℕ with all exact hypotheses explicit: a > 1, C > 0, C(n + 1) + D(n) = a(n) · C(n), D(n + 1) = a(n) · D(n), E is the centered state D − (a − 1)C, |E| < C, a uniform lower bound on E, and division-free normalized vanishing. It excludes persistent bounded negative behaviour and forces eventual centered defect zero; centered-zero plus an eventually nonzero next tail recovers Sylvester, but no reciprocal-tail irrationality follows. The unbounded negative mixed-sign branch and the prime-specific producer remain open. This is distinct from the periodic negative-orbit and cofinally bounded-negative no-go families; no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made, and no unrestricted #243 solution follows.

main_results.contribution_class: conditional analytic recovery criterion; novelty unassessed
main_results.statement: Under exact next-denominator and next-tail C/D dynamics with a, D : ℕ → ℤ, C : ℕ → ℕ, C > 0, the strict centered step equation, division-free normalized vanishing, and Summable normalized negative centered mass, the centered state vanishes eventually and a follows the Sylvester recurrence eventually.
main_results.boundary: This is a conditional recovery criterion: the source theorem assumes every displayed dynamics, positivity, strict centered-step, normalized-vanishing, and summability hypothesis, and does not prove them for the original Erdős #243 orbit. Any surviving canonical orbit must have divergent normalized negative mass. It supplies no prime-specific producer, unconditional #243 endpoint, or reciprocal-tail irrationality, and makes no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim. It is distinct from centered_state_dynamics, which uses a uniform lower-bound hypothesis rather than summability of normalized negative mass.

main_results.statement: An eventually periodic negative-error orbit with positive phase growth is impossible.
main_results.boundary: The theorem does not cover arbitrary unbounded negative behaviour.

main_results.statement: For every e >= 1, the complete dyadic totient kernel through level e has rational span dimension 2^e + 1.

claims.statement: For a finite integer coefficient family whose indices all lie in one quotient band k·d ≤ i_j < (k+1)·d, the factorial moment is exactly (d!)^k times the d-channel numerator. In the first band d ≤ i_j < 2d, channel cancellation forces the factorial moment to vanish; with all indices at least d and a nonzero moment, some index is therefore at least 2d.

Irrationality plus a separately supplied exact-modulus decay estimate therefore yields cofinal local-window escape. The decay estimate and irrationality input are not proved by this claim.

claims.statement: For every integer base b ≥ 2, an eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region has irrational series ∑ γ(a)/(b^a − 1). Excluding that terminating alternative implies irrationality. The terminating alternative is not excluded in general, so the full mixed-sign periodic-coefficient theorem is not claimed.

claims.statement: For the period-four signed weight 1,0,−1,0, the associated signed divisor coefficient vanishes for every n congruent to 3 modulo 4. A whole arithmetic progression can therefore carry zero coefficient, so residue-blind selection cannot force a protected nonzero residue for every periodic signed weight.

claims.statement: For every positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a·x is the coefficient at x, plus the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, plus an exact finite composite-dilation defect. For a finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet, the ray defect is bounded by the finite exceptional-frame cardinality plus the petal-support divisor count. For distinct primes and a residual argument coprime to their product, the two-layer operator on the support coefficient equals the iterated exact-prime-power pullback. The checked singleton {12} fixture has mixed (2²,3) layer value one at residual argument one. This is finite coefficient algebra only, with no decimation transport, bounded-Ω endpoint, or irrationality theorem.

For the half-greedy orbit, reduced and raw margins, three-depth take-run excess, primitive-lattice cap violation, support-coefficient tail gaps, and gcd-scaled predecessor overshoot are connected by exact identities and equivalences; cofinal supplies of the named witnesses imply that 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. claims.statement: Scalar-relation-invariant rational-linear channels have no nontrivial square determinant at any rank. Separately, a common coefficient word with a 1/0 seam and a common following overlap forces the terminal reverse-carry difference to be a power of two times an odd integer; a common nonnegative real carry bound yields the corresponding dyadic spacing inequality. The module neither supplies reverse-carry presentations nor a predecessor overlap, so it is not a greedy separation or irrationality theorem.

claims.statement: At an unresolved even seam, the scalar transition reaches exactly every integer terminal carry other than the one value 2*δ-c. The canonical seam-supply hypothesis is not proved.

claims.statement: The binary-scaled uncentred greedy half carry is antitone, and the square-root strip envelope divided by 2^N tends to zero. Therefore cofinal returns of the canonical greedy carry to that strip force the scaled carry to tend to zero and yield membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. The cofinal return hypothesis is not proved.
