terms.label: skill
terms.meaning_boundary: Skill means a recorded agent-operable procedure with triggers and constraints. It is not a personal talent, capability score, or permission grant.
terms.short_definition: In this system, a skill is a reusable set of instructions for carrying out a recognisable kind of task.
terms.reader_preview: In this system, a skill is a reusable set of instructions for carrying out a recognisable kind of task.
terms.card_definition: It states when it applies, the steps to follow, relevant constraints, and routes to governing material. Agents can discover and reuse it instead of reconstructing the workflow from scratch.
terms.reader_rule: A skill is procedural guidance; a component is implemented machinery that may carry out part of it.
terms.deep_definition: The skill should stay aligned with the tools and rules it names. An instruction pointing to an obsolete command needs repair even if its general advice remains sound.
terms.scope_note: Skills are the action vocabulary of the system, sitting alongside its components and doctrine. A reader meets them where the public pages describe how an agent works through a task, most directly on the page covering use with a coding agent.
terms.example: The procedure for working through a task with a coding agent is a skill: it names the situation it fits, lays out the steps to follow, and states the constraints that bound them, so the agent can run it without rederiving the workflow.

example_route.label: With a coding agent
example_route.gloss: see a skill that drives a coding agent through a task

terms.non_example: A skill is not a personal talent, a clever trick, or a feature being advertised. It is a recorded procedure with named triggers, defined steps, and stated limits that an agent runs.

relationships.gloss: Skills operationalize standards and doctrine.
Skill usage can reveal reusable refinements.

source_refs.gloss: Skill definition standard.

terms.label: slice
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A slice is a selected part of a larger collection or system.
terms.reader_preview: A slice is a selected part of a larger collection or system.
terms.card_definition: Plectis uses the word for bounded sets of files, records, or components included in a task or public release. Naming the selection makes it clear what can be inspected or changed.
terms.reader_rule: The selection's boundary should be explicit rather than inferred from its title.
terms.deep_definition: A public slice can be independently runnable while the wider system remains unpublished. Evidence about that slice applies to its included material and tested interactions, with any broader conclusions requiring additional support.
terms.scope_note: A slice establishes only what falls inside it. Nothing about the surrounding system follows from it.
terms.example: The public repository is a slice of the system it comes from: the components and their checks are inside the cut; the frontend, live tools, and non-public data are outside it.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: smoke check
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A smoke check is a quick test for major failures in basic operation.
terms.reader_preview: A smoke check is a quick test for major failures in basic operation.
terms.card_definition: It might confirm that an application starts, an example command runs, or a key page loads. The aim is to catch obvious breakage before investing in more detailed checks.
terms.reader_rule: A smoke check deliberately has limited coverage.
terms.deep_definition: Its success is a useful first signal, not a comprehensive assessment of correctness. Plectis should identify the basic behaviour exercised so readers can tell which further checks are needed for a particular change.
terms.scope_note: A smoke check establishes basic reachability, nothing deeper.
terms.example: A served-route smoke check confirms a page responds before its content is examined.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: smooth number
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A positive integer is y-smooth if none of its prime factors exceeds y.
terms.reader_preview: A positive integer is y-smooth if none of its prime factors exceeds y.
terms.card_definition: More generally, it is smooth over a specified set of primes if all its prime factors belong to that set. For example, 72 = 2³·3² is 3-smooth, while 70 has prime factors 2, 5, and 7.
terms.reader_rule: The bound or allowed prime set is part of the definition.
terms.deep_definition: The number 1 qualifies because it has no prime factors. The papers use smoothness to restrict which integers enter a sequence or reciprocal sum, often producing a structured but sparse collection.
terms.scope_note: Integer smoothness relative to a named bound or a named set of primes.
terms.example: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5 is {2,3,5}-smooth and is not 3-smooth, because 5 exceeds 3.
terms.non_example: A smooth curve in the plane is a geometric notion, not this arithmetic one.

terms.label: software
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: Software consists of programs and related data used by computers to perform tasks.
terms.reader_preview: Software consists of programs and related data used by computers to perform tasks.
terms.card_definition: On this site, the software section presents Plectis's reusable research components and the machinery supporting its workflow. It is distinguished from the mathematical reading routes, although formal proofs also use software tools.
terms.reader_rule: Each published component needs its own description, dependencies, and evidence.
terms.deep_definition: A repository can make implementation available without demonstrating every advertised use. The source, runnable example, and recorded check together help a reader assess the particular behaviour being claimed.
terms.scope_note: Software covers the named codebase, configuration, dependencies, and runtime boundary.
terms.example: Plectis publishes software components that readers can inspect and run locally.
terms.non_example: A screenshot or product description is not the software itself.

terms.label: source
terms.meaning_boundary: On a component card, source is the named committed path the claim is generated from. It is not any nearby link.
terms.short_definition: A source is the original or controlling material from which a particular claim or artifact is drawn.
terms.reader_preview: A source is the original or controlling material from which a particular claim or artifact is drawn.
terms.card_definition: Here it often means code, a structured record, a theorem declaration, or a document linked from a generated page. Which source matters depends on the question being asked.
terms.reader_rule: Source for implementation and source for human intent need not be the same material.
terms.deep_definition: A reliable explanation identifies the relevant source precisely, including a version where necessary. Opening it lets a reader check the detail that a summary may simplify or omit.
terms.scope_note: Public-card source paths and the repository-as-source-of-record rule.
terms.example: The specimen component names its source path beside its evidence class and scope limit.
terms.non_example: The nearest readable summary on the site is not automatically the source of a claim.

terms.label: source body
terms.meaning_boundary: The source body is the underlying code or document content. A public bundle may include a bounded copy, whose version and external dependencies determine what can be inspected or reproduced.
terms.short_definition: A source body is the actual content of the code or document being referenced.
terms.reader_preview: A source body is the actual content of the code or document being referenced.
terms.card_definition: In a component bundle, it can be the full function or module implementation, as distinct from its signature, description, path, or digest. Including the body makes direct inspection possible.
terms.reader_rule: The body needs an identifiable version and context to explain which material it represents.
terms.deep_definition: A function may also depend on imports, configuration, or other files outside its displayed body. The bundle should make those dependencies clear if readers are expected to reproduce its behaviour.
terms.scope_note: A source body makes the included implementation inspectable. It does not by itself establish correctness, behavior on untested inputs, equivalence with a private system, or authority over the data the code may process.
terms.example: A component's bundle copies its implementation into source_modules/ and re-runs it, so a passing check reflects the real body rather than a matching hash.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

Grounds this Plectis-specific definition and its scope.

terms.label: source file
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A source file contains material from which another artifact is built or defined.
terms.reader_preview: A source file contains material from which another artifact is built or defined.
terms.card_definition: Source files can be written by people or generated by tools. Their role as source is relative to the build or transformation being discussed.
terms.reader_rule: Being a source file does not automatically make it the editable authority for every workflow.
terms.deep_definition: Plectis identifies the owning source and builder so generated material can be refreshed correctly. Editing a generated source copy may be overwritten by the next update unless its upstream owner is changed.
terms.scope_note: A source file shows what the code says at the commit you are reading.
terms.example: Each component page opens its implementation directly, at a named path in the public repository.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: source slice
terms.meaning_boundary: A source slice is the explicitly selected public subset that backs Plectis’s pages and checks; it is not an arbitrary excerpt or a claim that the entire working system was exported.
terms.short_definition: A source slice is the explicitly selected source material included in a task, package, or public release.
terms.reader_preview: A source slice is the explicitly selected source material included in a task, package, or public release.
terms.card_definition: It can contain files and dependencies needed to support particular pages, components, or results. Plectis publishes bounded slices so readers can inspect relevant machinery without receiving the entire private working repository.

terms.short_definition: A subsum is a sum obtained by retaining selected terms of a series and omitting the others.
terms.reader_preview: A subsum is a sum obtained by retaining selected terms of a series and omitting the others.
terms.card_definition: If A is the selected index set, the expression is ∑ over n in A of aₙ. The resulting sequence of retained terms forms a subseries, whose sum must be defined when the selection is infinite.

terms.short_definition: Euler's totient φ(n) counts the integers from 1 through n that are coprime to the positive integer n.
terms.reader_preview: Euler's totient φ(n) counts the integers from 1 through n that are coprime to the positive integer n.
terms.card_definition: For example, φ(6) = 2 because only 1 and 5 are coprime to 6 in that range. The definition gives φ(1) = 1; for n greater than 1, the qualifying integers are all strictly smaller than n.
terms.reader_rule: The input must be a positive integer in this definition.
terms.deep_definition: The papers use the totient in arithmetic series. Its values encode how prime factors restrict coprimality, linking multiplicative structure with questions about sums and digit expansions.
terms.scope_note: A totient result covers the function as defined, not related functions.
terms.example: Erdős #249 asks whether the sum of the totient of n over two to the n is irrational.

terms.label: transcendental
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A number is transcendental if it is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients.
terms.reader_preview: A number is transcendental if it is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients.
terms.card_definition: Equivalently, it is not algebraic over the rational numbers. Familiar examples include π and e. Every real transcendental number is irrational, but some irrational numbers, such as √2, are algebraic.
terms.reader_rule: The polynomial must be nonzero: the zero polynomial vanishes at every number.
terms.deep_definition: Proving irrationality alone therefore does not establish transcendence. A transcendence argument must rule out every nonzero integer-coefficient polynomial relation, which is a stronger requirement than ruling out fractions.
terms.scope_note: Transcendence of one series says nothing about a related series until a proof connects them.
terms.example: Pi and e are transcendental; the square root of two is not.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: transcript
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A transcript is a textual record of speech or an interaction.
terms.reader_preview: A transcript is a textual record of speech or an interaction.
terms.card_definition: It can preserve what was said, typed, or reported during a session, sometimes with timings and speaker labels. Plectis uses transcripts as inspectable records and source material for later explanation.
terms.reader_rule: The recording method determines what the transcript captures and where errors may occur.
terms.deep_definition: Speech recognition can mishear words, and an interaction transcript may omit events outside the captured channel. Important quotations or claims should therefore be checked against the appropriate original recording or execution evidence.

terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: truth maintenance
terms.meaning_boundary: Truth maintenance records each claim’s evidence, dependencies, invalidators, and action consequences; it does not guarantee truth or replace the source that owns the claim.
terms.short_definition: Truth maintenance tracks claims together with their reasons and dependencies so they can be reconsidered when evidence changes.
terms.reader_preview: Truth maintenance tracks claims together with their reasons and dependencies so they can be reconsidered when evidence changes.
terms.card_definition: In AI and knowledge systems, this concerns managing beliefs and justifications. Plectis applies the idea to source records, checks, uncertainty, and decisions that depend on particular claims.
terms.reader_rule: Tracking a belief is not a guarantee that the belief is true.
terms.deep_definition: The useful behaviour is responding to a failed assumption or contradictory observation: identify affected conclusions, change their status, and review actions that relied on them rather than preserving an unsupported conclusion unchanged.
terms.scope_note: Truth maintenance covers how beliefs, evidence, and their dependencies are tracked across the system's control plane, separating receipts, model outputs, generated projections, and doctrine commitments so none borrows another's authority. A reader meets it wherever a claim is shown with its supporting evidence, its status, or the conditions under which it would be withdrawn.
terms.example: The Belief-State Process Reward Replay component is one concrete instance: it tracks a belief across a sequence of steps, scoring each step against what the belief should have been at that point and replaying the trajectory to see where a belief was wrongly held or wrongly dropped.

terms.non_example: Truth maintenance is not a guarantee that the system's beliefs are correct, and it is not a single switch that marks something true or false. It is the ongoing record of why each belief is held and what would change it.

terms.label: trying

terms.short_definition: Trying means attempting an action whose outcome is not yet established.
terms.reader_preview: Trying means attempting an action whose outcome is not yet established.
terms.card_definition: In research, an attempt can produce a proof, counterexample, useful failure, or no decisive result. Plectis keeps relevant evidence from attempts so later work can assess what was learned.
terms.reader_rule: The account should distinguish effort from the outcome actually obtained.
terms.deep_definition: A failed route is useful when its failure is explained precisely enough to guide another decision. Merely recording that an agent spent time on a task does not establish progress on the mathematical or software question.

terms.label: Type A

terms.reader_preview: Type A names an actor with direct access to the working system and permission to perform specified operations on it.

terms.label: Type A judgment
terms.meaning_boundary: Type A judgment is evidence- and doctrine-grounded discernment by an actor with live substrate access; it is not an intelligence rank, personality trait, or unrestricted license to change the system.

terms.reader_preview: Type A judgement is the practical reasoning an agent uses when acting on the live system.

terms.reader_preview: Type A metabolism names the maintenance work that requires judgement about the system's structure or rules.

terms.label: Type B
terms.meaning_boundary: Type B is ai_workflow's local no-private-substrate-authority classification. It is not a personality type, lower intelligence tier, capability grade, or synonym for every delegated worker.

terms.reader_preview: Type B names an actor reasoning from supplied or externally available context without direct authority over the working system.

terms.label: typed refusal
terms.meaning_boundary: A typed refusal is a local construct: an explicit, reason-carrying no-result when a computation cannot honestly produce a value. It is not a generic HTTP error.
terms.short_definition: A typed refusal is a structured result saying that an operation could not proceed, with a specific reason.
terms.reader_preview: A typed refusal is a structured result saying that an operation could not proceed, with a specific reason.
terms.card_definition: It distinguishes cases such as missing evidence, unsupported input, failed validation, or timeout. Plectis uses these categories so later work can choose a suitable response instead of receiving a plausible-looking invented value.
terms.reader_rule: The refusal reports the operation's limitation; it need not refute the underlying claim.
terms.deep_definition: A timeout, for example, means the check did not finish within its budget. It is different from the checker finding a counterexample or completing with a failure verdict.
terms.scope_note: Doctrine copy about honest failure.

terms.label: typed relation
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A typed relation is a connection that states how two identified items are related.
terms.reader_preview: A typed relation is a connection that states how two identified items are related.
terms.card_definition: In a mathematical map, the type might be implication, equivalence, finite instance, or obstruction. In system records, it might identify implementation, ownership, or a source relationship.
terms.reader_rule: The relation type and direction are part of the information being recorded.
terms.deep_definition: Two statements merely sharing a topic do not establish an implication between them. Plectis's mathematical edges need supporting evidence so navigation does not silently promote an association into a logical result.
terms.scope_note: A typed relation records an authored judgement about two statements.
terms.example: A directed edge labelled 'implies' from one statement node to another is a typed relation only when the implication and its direction have supporting evidence.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: unconditional result
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: An unconditional result needs no additional unresolved hypothesis beyond its stated mathematical setting.
terms.reader_preview: An unconditional result needs no additional unresolved hypothesis beyond its stated mathematical setting.
terms.card_definition: It still has definitions, domain restrictions, and logical foundations. The word distinguishes it from a result whose intended application depends on an open conjecture or other unestablished condition.
terms.reader_rule: Unconditional does not mean assumption-free or that the original research problem is fully solved.
terms.deep_definition: A proved equivalence or a theorem about a special case can be unconditional while the broader question remains open. The papers should say both what the result establishes and how it relates to the original target.
terms.scope_note: Unconditional does not mean assumption-free or that the original research problem is fully solved.
terms.example: Representative source: sites/microcosm/papers/source/plectis-erdos/paper/251/erdos-251-prime-gap-dyadic-series.tex::line 1038.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

terms.label: uniform convergence
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: Functions converge uniformly when one sufficiently late stage makes the error small simultaneously at every point of the stated domain.
terms.reader_preview: Functions converge uniformly when one sufficiently late stage makes the error small simultaneously at every point of the stated domain.
terms.card_definition: For every positive tolerance ε, there must be an N such that |fₙ(x) − f(x)| < ε for all n ≥ N and all x in the domain. The same N works for every x.
terms.reader_rule: Pointwise convergence instead allows the threshold N to depend on x.
terms.deep_definition: Uniform convergence preserves continuity of continuous functions in the usual metric setting. Passing strict inequalities or derivative bounds to a limit needs additional care; uniform convergence alone does not preserve every property.
terms.scope_note: Pointwise convergence instead allows the threshold N to depend on x.
terms.example: Representative source: sites/microcosm/papers/source/plectis-erdos/paper/1041/erdos-1041-lemniscate-newton-flow.tex::line 1076.
terms.non_example: Do not treat this glossary row as source authority; follow its source refs and evidence commands before making claims with the term.

source_refs.gloss: Published manuscript context for this mathematical term.

terms.label: uninterpretable
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: Here, uninterpretable describes work for which readers do not yet have an adequate account of what it says or why it works.
terms.reader_preview: Here, uninterpretable describes work for which readers do not yet have an adequate account of what it says or why it works.
terms.card_definition: A formal proof can check while its main idea, relationship to prior work, or intended meaning remains poorly explained. The missing task is to make that content understandable at an appropriate level of expertise.
terms.reader_rule: The term describes a current gap in understanding, not a proof that understanding is impossible.
terms.deep_definition: Useful exposition states the exact result, exposes the decisive argument, and preserves attribution and limits. Community understanding and use require further engagement beyond a machine's acceptance.
terms.scope_note: Names a result that cannot yet be explained by a person. Related cards: digestion, exposition, formal verification.
terms.example: A long kernel-accepted proof whose authors cannot say where the hard step was is uninterpretable in this sense.
terms.non_example: An informal argument that a reader can repair and restate is interpretable even before it is formalised.

terms.label: unit disc
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: The open unit disc is the set of complex numbers z with |z| < 1.
terms.reader_preview: The open unit disc is the set of complex numbers z with |z| < 1.
terms.card_definition: It consists of points at distance less than one from the origin in the complex plane. The closed unit disc uses |z| ≤ 1 and includes its boundary, the unit circle |z| = 1.
terms.reader_rule: Open and closed versions differ precisely at that boundary.
terms.deep_definition: The lemniscate papers use conditions such as |p(z)| < 1. That says the polynomial's value lies in the open unit disc; it does not necessarily say the input point z lies there.
terms.scope_note: Open unit disc in the complex plane unless a page specifies the closed disc.
terms.example: 0 and 1/2 are in the open unit disc; 1 and i are on the unit circle, so not inside it.
terms.non_example: A disc of radius 1 centred somewhere other than 0 is a different set.

terms.label: up-propagate
terms.meaning_boundary: Up-propagate means moving a reusable local lesson into the least-authoritative durable artifact that can honestly carry it; it does not promote every observation into doctrine.
terms.short_definition: To up-propagate is to place a reusable lesson in the shared source that should guide future relevant work.
terms.reader_preview: To up-propagate is to place a reusable lesson in the shared source that should guide future relevant work.
terms.card_definition: Plectis uses the move when a local correction reveals a missing rule, instruction, or relationship. The lesson is expressed with its evidence and limits, then attached to an existing owner such as a skill or standard.
terms.reader_rule: The appropriate destination is the narrowest one that can carry the supported lesson.
terms.deep_definition: This prevents repeated rediscovery without converting every local fix into a system-wide rule. The changed source should be discoverable through the workflow that needs it.
terms.scope_note: The term covers the upward movement of learning across the system's layers, from local tasks and signals up to skills, standards, paper modules, seeds, and axioms. A reader meets it in the doctrine and rules pages, particularly around the axiom on provenance propagation, and wherever the system explains how a local case improved a shared artifact.
terms.example: The axiom on provenance propagation and non-interference, AX-8, is a concrete instance: it states how a local lesson may be carried into a higher artifact while preserving where it came from and without disturbing the artifact it joins.

terms.label: validator
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A validator checks whether supplied material satisfies a declared set of requirements.
terms.reader_preview: A validator checks whether supplied material satisfies a declared set of requirements.
terms.card_definition: It can examine a schema, input constraints, relationships, or other properties and report a pass, failure, warning, or inability to complete. Plectis connects these outcomes to the rules being applied.

terms.deep_definition: A file may be structurally valid while containing a false claim, and a blocked validation may simply lack a dependency. Clear result categories help distinguish these situations and identify the next appropriate action.

terms.label: variable
terms.meaning_boundary: The glossary intends ordinary or domain usage. Repository-specific examples contextualize the term; they do not redefine it or certify one universal definition.
terms.short_definition: A variable is a symbol or name whose value is supplied, quantified, or allowed to vary within a stated setting.
terms.reader_preview: A variable is a symbol or name whose value is supplied, quantified, or allowed to vary within a stated setting.
terms.card_definition: In mathematics, n may range over natural numbers while x ranges over real numbers. In a program, a variable names a value held or computed during execution.
terms.reader_rule: The name alone does not determine its meaning or permitted values.
terms.deep_definition: This matters when reading formulas across papers: the same letter can denote different objects in different sections. Use the local definition and hypotheses rather than assigning a universal meaning to a familiar symbol.

terms.non_example: A fixed named constant is not varying merely because it is written with a letter.

terms.label: vibe-mathing
terms.meaning_boundary: Vibe-mathing is a coined phrase, by analogy with vibe coding: doing mathematics with an AI by steering on intuition and letting the model supply the working. No generally accepted external meaning is claimed.
terms.short_definition: “Vibe-mathing” is this project's informal name for accepting AI-generated mathematical reasoning on plausibility without adequate independent checking.
terms.reader_preview: “Vibe-mathing” is this project's informal name for accepting AI-generated mathematical reasoning on plausibility without adequate independent checking.
terms.card_definition: Intuition and conversation can help generate useful ideas, but a fluent argument may hide an invalid step. The failure occurs when generating a candidate is treated as establishing it.
terms.reader_rule: A proof needs verification appropriate to its statement, whether formal or carefully examined mathematical reasoning.
terms.deep_definition: The project's response is to keep claims, evidence, explanations, and unresolved steps distinct. Formal checking helps with encoded inference; it does not replace understanding the intended result or explaining its significance.
terms.scope_note: A coined local name for an informal way of working with an AI on maths. It is not a name for Lean-checked results.
terms.example: The earliest attempts at the Erdős problems here were vibe-mathing: long chats, confident arguments, and no kernel to refuse a bad step.
terms.non_example: A Lean-accepted theorem with a named remaining obligation is not vibe-mathing, even if an AI drafted the proof.

terms.label: wave
terms.meaning_boundary: Wave means a bounded execution grouping inside an ai_workflow phase. It is not a physical wave, market wave, social trend, or universal planning unit.
terms.short_definition: A wave is one bounded pass of work within a larger phase.
terms.reader_preview: A wave is one bounded pass of work within a larger phase.
terms.card_definition: It has a stated objective, execution approach, permitted scope, and expected result. Plectis uses waves to organise progress into units that can be inspected and incorporated into the continuing programme.
terms.reader_rule: The live work record determines which wave is active or complete.

terms.label: work landing
terms.meaning_boundary: Work landing is a local ai_workflow construct for accepting one bounded change into durable substrate. It does not imply that unrelated follow-up work is complete or that the phrase is generally standardized.
terms.short_definition: Work landing is the point at which an attempted change becomes a recorded, accepted part of the system.
terms.reader_preview: Work landing is the point at which an attempted change becomes a recorded, accepted part of the system.

terms.label: working record
terms.meaning_boundary: In Plectis, a working record is a long rendered reasoning-surface PDF for one mathematical problem; it is not an ordinary worklog, a complete private agent trace, or the shorter problem note.
terms.short_definition: A working record is the detailed account of research on one problem, preserving results, attempts, evidence, and unresolved questions.

terms.reader_rule: Different passages can have different evidence status, so the record should identify what is proved, computed, cited, or open.
terms.deep_definition: Its purpose is to help another reader understand and continue the work. Preserving an attempted argument does not endorse it once a later correction or counterexample has been recorded.
terms.scope_note: A working record covers the selected reasoning, checked premises, failed routes, and surviving obligation presented in that rendered version. It is not proof authority, a complete private search history, or a generic contemporaneous project log.

terms.label: workingness
terms.meaning_boundary: Workingness is a local diagnostic posture about observed operation. It is not a standardized reliability metric and does not imply whole-system correctness.
terms.short_definition: Workingness is Plectis's term for whether its evidence, beliefs, uncertainty, and permitted actions remain coherently connected.
terms.reader_preview: Workingness is Plectis's term for whether its evidence, beliefs, uncertainty, and permitted actions remain coherently connected.
terms.card_definition: It asks what the system currently claims, what supports those claims, what could invalidate them, and how decisions respond to missing or contradictory evidence. Passing tests are one input to that assessment.
terms.reader_rule: The term names a proposed evaluative idea, not a universal measure of reliability.
terms.deep_definition: Its value depends on concrete records and behaviour: an unsupported claim should change status, and an action depending on it should be reconsidered rather than silently proceeding.
terms.scope_note: Workingness covers the system's epistemic health as a whole, distinct from ordinary event logging. A reader meets it wherever a result is being interpreted before a change is made: an evidence page showing what a pass proves, a drift check, or a live receipt. The owning module is the Workingness Instrument, and any dossier is a readable projection of that state.

terms.non_example: Workingness is not a green test suite or a build-passing badge. A run can be entirely green and still have low workingness if the system cannot say what remains unknown, what would change its mind, or which actions it is allowed to take.

terms.label: Workingness Instrument
terms.meaning_boundary: A workingness instrument binds one live result to evidence, invalidators, and allowed or blocked actions; it is not a monitoring dashboard, a correctness verdict, or an authority writer.

terms.reader_preview: A Workingness Instrument is a proposed structured record connecting one outcome to its evidence, dependencies, and permitted next actions.
terms.card_definition: It describes the claim, current status, possible invalidation conditions, unresolved disputes, and relevant repairs. The purpose is to make the consequences of a result explicit instead of leaving them in informal judgement.
terms.reader_rule: The record's existence does not establish that every described control has been implemented.
terms.deep_definition: For an implemented instance, source and execution evidence must show how changes in the record affect the actions that depend on it. The governing material identifies the current design and supported scope.
terms.scope_note: The term covers the governing record that binds evidence, judgment, appeals, repairs, and mutation permissions for a single live claim. A reader meets it where the site shows how a passing or failing result is allowed to act on the system, and a summary dossier may stand in front of it.

headline_results.what_this_is: Work on eight unsolved Erdős problems: #68, #243, #249, #251, #257, #269, #1041, and #1049. All eight remain open; none is solved here. #249 and #257 are the two reviewed core programmes carrying the curated claims registry below; the other six are problem-owned expansion lanes whose per-problem authority is the problems index. What exists is a body of exact reductions, unconditional finite exclusions, structural theorems and machine-checked supporting mathematics, each stated at its own strength -- plus, for #269, a two-prime transcendence result established by a paper argument using Bugeaud-Laurent, deliberately not a Lean theorem, recorded as such in its problem row.

per_problem.question: Is the series sum_{n >= 2} 1/(n! - 1) irrational?
what_is_checked: The exact integral normal form: the series is irrational if and only if the strict factorial successor Z_m misses divisibility by m cofinally.
The equivalent carry form: rationality is equivalent to eventual unit carry, so cofinally many non-unit carries imply irrationality.
Canonical factorial digits, exact remainder recurrences, zero-tail propagation, and the divisor-factorial centre recurrence.
Integral channel congruences, the lcm tax, the prime unit translator, and factorial-grid Cramer residual identities.
Weighted projection and factor-split rigidity consumers with their exact modular and Archimedean hypotheses.
The zero-plateau and first-exit carry dichotomy, prime-power prefix obstructions, and exact doubled-prime branch characterisations.
A Lean-checked implication from one exact non-unit carry to a rational-denominator lower bound; an independently regenerated exact GMP certificate at m = 300000 supplies the finite input.
what_is_not_checked: Irrationality of the factorial-denominator series.
A theorem producing cofinally many divisibility misses or non-unit carries.
Cofinal strict nonintegrality of the factorial-grid Cramer residual.
The weighted collision-product and complementary-residue estimates needed by the factor-split projection consumer.
The GMP computation is an exact finite external certificate, not a Lean evaluation and not an unbounded argument.

open_obligations.statement: On an unbounded family of tailored prime blocks, prove both the weighted collision-core product bound and the independent complementary-residue inequality consumed by the exact unit-factor scale split.
At infinitely many genuinely nonterminal indices, prove quantitative repeated-support valuation amplification strong enough to meet the checked endpoint inequality.
For infinitely many primes, force the reduced predecessor gap outside the exact lower unit-carry cylinder.
For infinitely many odd primes, rule out both exact p^2-divisibility branches at index 2p by coupling the carry value to the predecessor residue.

Construct an unbounded factorial-grid family whose exact Cramer residual is nonintegral, using a determinant, valuation, cancellation, or gcd-of-minors certificate that controls the finite sign-changing block.

per_problem.question: Under a rapid-growth hypothesis on an integer sequence, does rationality of its reciprocal sum force the sequence to satisfy the Sylvester recurrence eventually?
what_is_checked: The exact product-cleared tail dynamics and the defect identity, as identities in the integer state variables.
That a vanishing centred state is absorbing under strict centring, so the state is either eventually zero or nowhere zero.
That eventual vanishing of the centred state, with the next tail state nonvanishing, forces the Sylvester recurrence eventually.
That a nonnegative centred state vanishes eventually, by descent.
That the centred state cannot be eventually constant and negative, at any magnitude and any common scale.
That the negative magnitude cannot be eventually periodic with positive drift, in the regime where each magnitude is below its multiplier.
A coprimality barrier: a sequence tending to infinity with uniformly bounded upward increments cannot permanently avoid infinitely many fresh pairwise coprime moduli.
That a reduced exact tail has pairwise coprime multipliers which its numerator permanently avoids, so no such tail has a divergent numerator with bounded rise.
That the tail gcd stabilises under cofinally bounded negative magnitudes.
Conditionally: exact dynamics, eventual strict centring, an eventually bounded negative part, and normalised vanishing together force the centred state to vanish eventually.
That survival through a fixed number of forced updates depends only on the initial state modulo a factorial of the horizon.
what_is_not_checked: The unrestricted problem.

That eventual strict centring and normalised vanishing follow from the growth hypothesis and rationality. Both are assumed by the final theorem and neither is derived, so that theorem constrains the state system rather than the original sequence.
Any exclusion of negative excursions whose magnitudes are unbounded along a cofinal set.
The criterion of Erdos and Straus and Duverney's conditional characterisation, which are cited rather than formalised and are both stronger than anything checked here.

open_obligations.statement: Exclude, or construct, an exact orbit whose centred state is negative infinitely often with magnitudes unbounded along that cofinal set. Every checked exclusion consumes some finiteness: a fixed set of prime divisors, a fixed period, or a fixed bound on the negative part.
Derive eventual strict centring and normalised vanishing from the growth hypothesis and rationality, or show that they do not follow.
Kernel-check the Erdos-Straus weighted criterion and Duverney's conditional characterisation under explicit analytic hypotheses.

per_problem.question: Is the dyadic series sum p_n/2^n over consecutive primes irrational? Equivalently, is the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series irrational?
what_is_checked: The finite summation-by-parts identity relating the prime dyadic partial sums to the prime-gap dyadic partial sums, with an exact endpoint term and no convergence premise.
The factor-of-two normalisation between the two displayed indexings, at every finite horizon.
Conditional on summability of the prime dyadic series, the exact infinite prime-gap identity and the equivalence of irrationality of the prime and prime-gap series.
For an abstract integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence: the exact block identity, and that a shift of fixed length is integral exactly when an explicit scaled state is.
That one integral shift propagates to every later index.
That repeated doubling removes the power-of-two denominator, so every rational-valued dyadic recurrence has one fixed positive shift integral at all sufficiently late indices.
For a real-valued dyadic recurrence, cofinal non-integrality of every fixed positive shift implies irrationality of the initial state.
That the actual consecutive-prime-gap sequence is unbounded, by the factorial prime-free-interval construction, and therefore is not eventually periodic with any positive period.
For any integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence, two adjacent fixed-length shifts lying strictly between -1 and 1 cannot both be integral when the corresponding digits differ.
For the actual prime gaps, a cofinal supply of adjacent small-shift pairs with a mismatching gap excludes eventual integrality of that fixed shift.
The generic distance-to-integers core of the finite-truncation criterion: an approximation farther than its error bound from every integer certifies non-integrality.
what_is_not_checked: The target irrationality.

The definition and recurrence of the concrete prime-gap tail as Lean infinite sums; the note supplies these at paper level. Summability of the concrete prime series is Lean-checked unconditionally via an elementary polynomial prime bound.
A theorem supplying cofinally many adjacent actual-prime-gap tail shifts in the open unit interval with the required gap mismatch.
Any theorem forcing periodicity or automaticity of the prime gaps from rationality; the free-carry identity disconfirms that route.

open_obligations.statement: For every fixed h >= 1 and every N0, find N >= N0 for which sum_{j>=1} (g_{N+h+j}-g_{N+j})/2^j is not an integer.

For every fixed h >= 1 and every N0, find N >= N0 such that both adjacent full tail shifts have absolute value less than 1 and g_{N+h+1} != g_{N+1}. The checked local consumer then excludes eventual integrality of the h-shift.

Formalise summability of the actual prime and prime-gap dyadic series and identify the concrete infinite prime-gap tail with the checked real/rational dyadic recurrence, so the local consumer reaches the target series without a paper-only analytic bridge.

per_problem.question: For a monic polynomial whose roots lie in the open unit disc, must two roots be joinable by a curve of length less than two inside the open unit lemniscate?
what_is_checked: Along a trajectory tangent to the complex Newton vector field -f/f', the polynomial value satisfies w' = -w.
The exponentially rescaled polynomial value is a first integral, so the value of a Newton trajectory remains on one oriented ray.
A finite Newton-flow connection can only join endpoints whose polynomial values lie on the same positive ray; distinct critical-value arguments therefore exclude such a connection.
For two translated critical values, the ray-collision locus is a real affine line with an exact one-parameter description.
A finite family of ray-collision lines can be avoided by an arbitrarily small common translation.
An explicit root-retention estimate keeps roots of a sufficiently small constant perturbation inside the unit disc.

A repair of Proposition 12 that retains the printed 1/(2π) spanning-tree coefficient; any later argument must change the metric inequality.
A perturbation theorem that first makes critical values injective while preserving the relevant lemniscate component, collars, and strict length slack.
The global planar decomposition and metric gluing needed to obtain a curve of length less than two.

per_problem.question: For which rational bases is the corresponding series irrational? The smallest resistant explicit base is three halves.
what_is_checked: That a literal coordinatewise transfer of the integer-base clearing argument forces a power-versus-linear inequality, and that this inequality is impossible at base three halves.
The exact denominator-cleared rational-base tail recurrence, including its forcing term.
That for every noninteger base with denominator at least two the forcing magnitude grows at least exponentially, while at denominator one it collapses to a bounded expression.
The complete elementary Archimedean height inequality used by the published Bundschuh-Väänänen criterion at base seven halves; the analytic irrationality theorem itself remains external.
Polynomial bounds on the doubled denominator exponents in the homogenised Padé construction, together with an exact gap identity.
The exact exterior-determinant elimination identity, and that rowwise contents scale the Padé errors, exterior determinant, and absolute determinant height by the same factors.
The exact Heine-Zudilin cone endpoint exponent arithmetic used to identify the bottom and top coefficient endpoints.
That homogeneous evaluation at (3,2) sees only the constant endpoint modulo three and the top endpoint modulo two, so unit endpoints obstruct common local factors.

That under unit top and constant endpoint hypotheses, a common multiplier of the two specialised coefficient channels is divisible by neither two nor three; the missing local gain must therefore survive primitive normalisation.
That vanishing of the higher bottom and top endpoint jets is exactly divisibility by the corresponding powers of three and two.
That the source integer-base ratio inequality implies a strictly negative scalar product-formula margin at three halves.

That the four-jet target has exact cardinality (3^R)^2(2^S)^2 and, for positive R, any family with n at least 4R+2S forces two distinct binary selectors to collide; their {-1,0,1} difference cancels all four endpoint jets.
That the rectangular Hermite-Pade threshold never improves on the classical one in the checked exponent model, with equality characterised exactly.
The exact 81/200 height region: 31/4 and every positive power lie inside it and outside the earlier Bundschuh-Vaananen region, while 3/2 lies outside both.

At n = 0, the Amdeberhan-Zeilberger q-Apery operator applied to Van Assche's moving diagonal has residual -p(p-1)^2(p+1)(p^5+2p^4+2p^3+2p^2+2), which is strictly negative and nonzero for every real p > 1.
what_is_not_checked: The universal rational-base conjecture, including the case 3/2, remains open. The 31/4 power family has an ordinary proof in the paper; it is not an end-to-end Lean theorem.
The published analytic height theorem, which is cited and used as an external result and is not formalised here.
The all-scale Heine-Zudilin coefficient construction at rational base three halves; the primary source assumes an integer base.
The source analytic irrationality theorem inside the 81/200 height region; only its elementary parameter specialisations are formalised.
A sufficiently large primitive-normalised, non-collapsed coefficient family meeting the checked n >= 4R+2S threshold at the required quadratic depths.
That one of the resulting bounded-coefficient collision vectors has a nonzero polynomial pair, lies outside the analytic remainder nullspace, and has sufficient local gain.
Positivity or decay of the elementary Padé remainder; only its exponent arithmetic is checked.

Any general recurrence, endpoint, lattice, valuation, denominator, or irrationality conclusion from the n = 0 q-Apery residual; it proves only that the named scalar recurrence does not transfer to Van Assche's diagonal.

open_obligations.statement: After dividing every coefficient pair by its rowwise common content, at positive quadratic target depths R_n,S_n exhibit at least 4R_n+2S_n primitive coefficient pairs from a genuinely non-collapsed deformation, prove that the required two-adic and three-adic gain survives primitive normalisation, and prove that at least one resulting checked {-1,0,1} collision has a nonzero polynomial pair and lies outside the analytic remainder nullspace; or prove an exact rank obstruction.

per_problem.claim_registry_status: not_registered; the claim registry does not carry these declarations and kernel checking them does not promote them into reviewed public claims

headline_results.status_counts_reading: These are registry statuses, not quality grades. 'proved here' means a Lean proof term is accepted for that statement; 'conditional reduction' means an exact equivalence whose two sides may both remain open; 'unconditional progress' means an unconditional theorem about the open problem itself.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Unbounded and non-eventually-periodic consecutive prime gaps
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The consecutive-prime-gap sequence is unbounded and is not eventually periodic with any positive period. These coefficient facts do not by themselves imply irrationality of the prime-gap or prime-index dyadic series.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite Newton-flow ray separation and perturbation consumer
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: An explicit exponential-decay Newton connection can occur only when its endpoint values lie on the same positive ray; conversely, every finite injective complex family admits an arbitrarily small common translation making all values nonzero and all positive-ray arguments distinct. These are finite perturbative and conditional connection statements.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Quotient-band channel breakpoint for factorial moments
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a finite integer coefficient family whose indices all lie in one quotient band k·d ≤ i_j < (k+1)·d, the factorial moment is exactly (d!)^k times the d-channel numerator. In the first band d ≤ i_j < 2d, channel cancellation forces the factorial moment to vanish; with all indices at least d and a nonzero moment, some index is therefore at least 2d.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite least-positive-residue contradiction for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a positive modulus C, a positive integer state c bounded by K cannot be congruent to x modulo C when the canonical least-positive representative of x is greater than K; the zero residue class is represented by C. The integer carry form and exact residue classifier are checked in Lean.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite #269 radix prefixes admit an altered rational completion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Every finite positive integral radix prefix with nonnegative integral digits extends to a positive rational orbit by changing the future to radix 2 and digit 1. In particular, the actual word through any finite horizon has such an abstract completion. This is a countermodel to finite-prefix-only inference and is not a rational model of the actual infinite smooth-number series.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Size-authenticated bounded certificate checks for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The bounded width and cumulative-array checkers expose their size hypotheses, are sound on every accessed entry, compose across adjacent ranges, and carry explicit regressions showing that default-zero array access, half-height cancellation, and finite coverage cannot certify an infinite/cofinal conclusion. No paper numerical table is executed or validated by these safety theorems alone.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Canonical quotient-greedy and scaled-remainder frontier at 1/21
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Membership of 1/21 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent both to excluding one explicit fatal/cofinite/aligned branch and to cofinally bounded scaled actual greedy remainders. Every closed Boolean quotient row is the deterministic quotient-greedy row; any unbounded sequence of canonical rows with remainder at most 2^R gives membership. On the complementary fatal branch the remainder is eventually strictly supercapacity, the boundary rank is always selected, and support and remainder follow one exact affine recurrence. A final skipped exponent also forces a structured one-sided approximation to the Erdős–Borwein constant with exact denominator-order constraints. These results isolate permanent affine supercapacity as the surviving late regime; they do not contradict it or prove 1/21 membership.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Explicit basis of the dyadic totient kernel span
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Lean constructs an explicit odd-core-indexed basis of the rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel, with exact span equality and linear independence. This is an independent constructive proof route; its infinite-dimensionality consequence is not an independent contribution because Coons's non-2-regularity theorem already implies it.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Dyadic totient-kernel finite-level rank
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every e, a CRT–Dirichlet construction produces a separated nonzero evaluation minor for the canonical dyadic totient-kernel family, which is linearly independent with exact span dimension 2^e + 1. The same Lean development proves that the full dyadic kernel span is not finite-dimensional, but that corollary is not an independent contribution: it is equivalent, for this integer-valued sequence module, to Coons's non-2-regularity theorem. Even residues reduce to odd-core channels, and the compressed-adjoint boundary remains available. These coefficient-side theorems do not prove that S is irrational.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Campbell shift-synchronization strategy boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Campbell's application of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate chooses delta = 1/4, so at prime-search height X the progression modulus d must satisfy d <= X^(1/4), equivalently d^4 <= X. In the proposed last-skip synchronization, P is the fatal-window prime cap, t the unavoidable phase period, and d the combined progression modulus. Taking X = P, the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, and d^4 <= P are inconsistent. The shifted-zero interface is guarded by a putative last skip and is exactly equivalent to infinitely many actual greedy skips and to membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. It is an endpoint restatement, not an independent Campbell input, and proves no half-membership.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go theorem
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At every fixed positive precision, every finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols admits a compatible carry orbit from an arbitrary incoming integer state, with each successive state within the corresponding valuation-unit radius. Thus bounded local signatures alone cannot exclude all finite centred endpoints; growing precision or global information remains necessary for an endpoint argument.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: LCM factor-ideal anchor-pulse no-go theorem
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every t ≥ 3, a nonzero synthetic affine carry has forcing letters in the principal ideal generated by φ(lcm(1,…,t)), matches every stated whole-ray anchor, and remains within the diagonal bounds while its state is a strict survivor. The same countermodel survives every finite integer shift polynomial. Thus factor ideals, whole-ray anchors, and finite-rank shift algebra alone do not force carry escape. The construction does not assert that its forcing letters are actual totient differences and does not rule out nonlinear use of fresh divisor channels.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Actual LCM positive corridor and top-edge boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a ≥ 8 and J + (a + 6) < 2·2^a, the true translated LCM-orbit difference is strictly positive. If it is represented by an integer and the dyadic modulus has room for the directed endpoint strip, the carry survivor is strictly negative and the discrepancy residue is exactly the top-edge representative 2^K − carry_K, strictly between the strip’s lower edge and 2^K. Thus the positive corridor eliminates the nonnegative true survivor but does not itself produce a central-band contradiction; an independent arithmetic exclusion of the top boundary is still required.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Base 3/2 coordinatewise corridor exclusion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: With N ≥ 1 and K ≥ 1, the six-condition CoordinatewiseCorridor at base 3/2 is impossible for every natural Q and digit. This excludes only that literal coordinatewise clearing architecture, not rationality or irrationality of F(3/2) or any other proof architecture.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact rational-base cleared-tail recurrence
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For rational r, s, B, and F, a coefficient sequence coeff : ℕ → ℚ, and r ≠ 0, the denominator-cleared tail state satisfies rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) (N + 1) = r · rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) N − B · coeff (N + 1) · s^(N + 1) for every N. The identity is not derived from rationality and is not itself a rationality contradiction.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Rational-base forcing-term growth boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural s, B, coeff, and N, if s ≥ 2, B ≥ 1, and coeff(N + 1) ≥ 1, then rationalBaseForcingNat s B coeff N ≥ 2^(N + 1); at s = 1 the same quantity is exactly B · coeff(N + 1). This is an elementary forcing-term bound, not a bounded-state contradiction or endpoint result.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Van Assche q-Apéry diagonal recurrence non-transfer
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every real p > 1, the n = 0 residual obtained by applying the Amdeberhan–Zeilberger q-Apéry operator to Van Assche's moving diagonal is the displayed strictly negative factorisation, hence is nonzero. This rules out that selected diagonal for that recurrence at n = 0; it proves no general recurrence, endpoint, or #1049 irrationality result.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Bounded-rise fresh-modulus coprimality barrier
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural sequences u and m, if u tends to infinity with upward increments bounded by a fixed positive B, the moduli m are eventually greater than 1 and pairwise coprime, and each earlier m(i) is coprime to every later u(t), then the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is a reusable state-level obstruction, not a proof of the full Erdős #243 assertion.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Eventually-periodic negative-orbit exclusion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural sequences a, D, C, and e with 2 ≤ a(n), positive e(N+n) < a(N+n), the exact recurrences D(n+1) = a(n)·D(n) and C(n+1) = C(n) + e(n), the shape equation D(n) + e(n) = (a(n)−1)·C(n), and a positive-period, positive-drift tail e(N+n+h) = e(N+n) and C(N+n+h) = C(N+n) + M with h > 0 and M > 0, the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is only the eventually-periodic negative-magnitude obstruction; mixed-sign and unbounded-negative behaviour remain outside the claim and the full Erdős #243 endpoint remains open.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Phase-specific density obstruction for the two cubic survivor profiles
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For either surviving cubic profile Q_{12,c}(n)=2n(n+1)(n+2)+c with c=1 or c=-1, the exact tail recurrences force a mismatch in every sufficiently late four-index window at the corresponding phase modulo 7. The mismatch set therefore has lower density at least 1/7, and hence at least the 1/28 stated in the long paper. No phase-free or arbitrary-profile density statement is claimed.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite-support denominator period noncollapse
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every finite nonempty support F with 0 ∉ F and integer base b ≥ 2, the reduced denominator of the literal finite sum ∑_{n∈F} 1/(bⁿ−1) is coprime to b and the multiplicative order of b modulo that denominator equals F.lcm id. This finite-support theorem supplies no unbounded support certificate and does not settle the universal infinite-support Erdős #257 endpoint.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Weighted-phase carry split and finite realised span for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The exact weighted-phase carry recurrence splits into a finite residue digit, each of the two coordinates staying inside its declared interval, and an integral quotient coboundary that is not controlled. An explicit factorisation through a finite-dimensional function-faithful observer then forces the realised symbolic span to be finite. Nothing here proves a finite-state quotient or a literal infinite realised span, and no rationality or irrationality conclusion follows.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact finite arithmetic and run-threshold checks for #249
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The four displayed discrepancy values at (h,X,L)=(1,4,9), their finite room and certified kills, the Farey denominator bound, and the corrected finite run threshold hold exactly. These finite facts do not supply a cofinal certificate producer.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Generic centering countermodel for the #249 decomposition
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: A two-point complex model has vanishing peripheral mean contributions while its centered contribution remains nonzero. This refutes the generic inference from peripheral cancellation to a centered budget; it is not a counterexample to the arithmetic totient-centered predicate.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: One unconditional finite first-harmonic gap instance
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At (h,X,L)=(1,4,9), the exact finite first-harmonic expression has the certified norm gap bounded by 21X/25. This is one finite instance and does not establish DTWFirstHarmonicNormGap or any cofinal statement.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Full-support Erdős–Borwein irrationality, every integer base b ≥ 2
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every integer b ≥ 2, the series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational (Erdős, 1948).

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: The Erdős–Borwein constant E is irrational
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: E = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) is irrational, as the base-2 corollary of the full-support theorem.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Named infinite-support irrationality families toward #257
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every base b ≥ 2, ∑_{n∈A} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational for factorial support, power-of-two support, multiples, pairwise-coprime supports with summable reciprocals, eventually-periodic supports, residue classes, and the odd numbers. Proved families, not the universal statement.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Unconditional denominator exclusion for the totient constant
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is not equal to p/q for any integer p and any 1 ≤ q ≤ 79 639 646 646 701 375 323 355 774 875 831 053 (≈ 7.96 × 10³⁴). A lower bound on any rational representation, not a proof of irrationality.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact reduction of #249 to finite decidable certificates
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: S is irrational if and only if certified non-integrality witnesses occur at unbounded parameters. The pointwise completeness theorem and the diagonal supply theorem together show that an unbounded lcm-diagonal supply is equivalent as well. Producing that supply remains open.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Certificate completeness
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At fixed parameters, a certified kill exists exactly when the corresponding tail difference is non-integral. At every positive shift, integrality of one tail difference forces S to be rational; thus irrationality is equivalent to pointwise non-integrality, and to pointwise finite certificates.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Initial certified-kill segment and generated certificates
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Kernel-checked certified kills for the listed small periods, every lcm-diagonal scale t ≤ 82, and the finite certificate shards. The historical 28 explicit deposits through t = 64 form a strict subset of this contiguous finite band.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact full-target reduction on the lcm diagonal
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At each lcm-diagonal scale, integrality is equivalent to a foreign-defect term landing in an explicit full-target interval. Globally, S is irrational if and only if the full target is avoided at arbitrarily large diagonal scales; that cofinal avoidance is not proved.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Scalar-localisation height obstruction
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: If H divides the reduced denominator of a rational x and the reduced denominator of c·x divides H for an integer c, then the complementary factor x.den/H divides |c|. Scalar localisation transfers, rather than discards, that denominator information; this local obstruction is not an irrationality criterion.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: All-base totient-kernel reduction, spanning, and conditional rank
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every integer base k at least 2, Lean checks the zero-residue scaling identity, the exact nonzero scalar used in composite-base residue reduction, unique quotient/nonzero-digit coordinates, and cardinality k^e + 1 of the canonical finite-level index. It proves unconditionally that this canonical family spans the complete kernel through level e, and proves exact rank k^e + 1 under the explicit hypothesis that the family is linearly independent. Lean does not prove that hypothesis or formalise Martin's positive-density theorem; the unconditional basis and rank theorem in the paper uses Martin externally.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Sublogarithmic divisor-coverage zero windows
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: A rational support-series value forces every zero window in the divisor-count coefficient to have length at most ε·log₂(N+1) + B, where B ≥ 0 is built from ε, c and v but is bound after the support and numerator, so no single constant is claimed uniform across supports. This constrains coverage; it does not solve universal #257.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Greedy geometry of the Mersenne achievement set
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, perfect, totally disconnected, nowhere dense, and has Lebesgue measure one. Membership is equivalent to greedy survival at every level; for the target 1/2 it is exactly equivalent to the canonical greedy orbit omitting infinitely many exponents. No finite normalized support has value 1/2, so positive membership would automatically produce an infinite rational-valued support and refute universal #257. Finite exact-rational death certificates soundly prove non-membership (3/4 is excluded at level one). The strict-tail Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovač–Tao; no novelty claim is made for the formalised refinements.

remaining_open_propositions.statement: Prove that S = ∑_{n≥2} 1/(n! − 1) is irrational.
Prove that S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is irrational, with no bound on a possible rational denominator.
Prove that Π = ∑_{n≥1} p_n/2ⁿ is irrational; the exact tail-shift equivalence and prime-gap constraints do not supply the required cofinal escape.
Produce certified non-integrality witnesses at unbounded parameters. A sufficient one-parameter form is to produce them along the lcm diagonal.
Decide whether 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set. Yes refutes universal #257; no closes only this route.

Decide the exact 1/21 branch: equivalently, exclude the fatal/cofinite/aligned branch, contradict its eventual permanent affine-supercapacity recurrence, prove cofinally bounded scaled greedy remainders, or force an unbounded sequence of closed canonical quotient rows. A positive membership result would refute universal #257; no such producer is proved.
Prove irrationality for every infinite support A, not only the named support families formalised here.

Determine irrationality of the running-LCM reciprocal sum for finite prime sets of size at least three. For {2,3,5}, the rationality-to-carry bridge is established and cofinal local-window escape remains open.
Find or refute the required short curve between two roots inside the open lemniscate; finite ray separation and perturbative root retention do not supply the global topology and length argument.

Determine whether F(t) = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(tⁿ − 1) is irrational for every rational t > 1. F(31/4) is an ordinary Zudilin specialization, not a Lean theorem; the 3/2 approximant with remainder control and the universal assertion remain open.

Prove the Erdős #243 assertion: if 1 ≤ a₁ < a₂ < ··· has aₙ/aₙ₋₁² → 1 and rational reciprocal sum, then aₙ = aₙ₋₁² − aₙ₋₁ + 1 eventually; the checked barrier does not settle the mixed-sign unbounded regime.
Prove that B·T_a ∉ ℤ for every B ≥ 1 coprime to 30 and every a ≥ 1.
Prove that for every B ≥ 1 coprime to 30 and every a₀ ≥ 1 there are ℓ ≥ a₀ and h ≥ 1 with lpr_{W(ℓ,h)}(−B·F(ℓ,h)) > K(B, ℓ+h), where K is the defined long-paper cap.

Represent D_{2,3,5} faithfully by a specified two-dimensional Mahler-type value theorem with every hypothesis verified, give a conditional theorem under explicit logarithmic nondegeneracy, or prove no such representation exists.
Decide whether every nonterminal canonical orbit of the reduced-orbit problem has limsup_n (log M_n)/n > 0, equivalently 2^n ≤ M_n^K infinitely often for some K ≥ 1.
Decide whether, for each h ≥ 1, some s ≥ 1 and 0 < η < 1 give, for every X₀, admissible X and L meeting the displayed size conditions for which the four first-harmonic bounds hold.
Decide whether the scaled actual greedy remainder returns cofinally to one bounded interval: whether some B < ∞ has 2^N r_N ≤ B at arbitrarily large N.
Decide whether a bounded-memory 2-adic or discrepancy invariant of the actual support forces a closed return or forbids permanent supercapacity, or prove no such invariant exists.
Decide whether the final-skip signatures prove |E − a_M| ≥ gap_M, contradicting 0 < a_M − E < gap_M, for E = ∑_{n≥1}(2^n − 1)^{−1} and the last-skip approximant a_M.

headline_results.how_to_read_this: Each statement is quoted at exactly the strength the registry asserts, including its own negative clause. Do not add a hedge that the statement does not contain, and do not drop one that it does. If you conclude from this packet that the mathematics is thin or unverifiable, name which of these statements you checked and found wanting -- a general impression formed without opening one is not a finding about the work. One exception, added when this build learned to check it: where mathematical_assertions records a fidelity finding against a claim, the registry sentence is the surface that is wrong, and those claims are listed under withheld_from_this_list rather than quoted here.
headline_results.verification_boundary: No Lean kernel ran during this build. These are registry statuses and source coordinates, so a reader can locate and check each proof; that is a route to verification, not verification itself.

withheld_from_this_list.why: This build compares every public sentence against the theorem it cites. These claims are real results whose registry sentence asserts more than the cited surface proves, so quoting them here would put the overstatement on the packet's most quotable page.
withheld_from_this_list.not_a_retraction: Withheld from a first-contact list is not withdrawn. The mathematics stands at the strength the theorem proves; it is the registry sentence that needs correcting, and the correction is in /upstream_defects.

type_b_orientation.what_the_hell_this_is: Plectis is an open-source mathematics project. Its primary repository, plectis-erdos, carries research on eight still-open Erdős problems: formal source, partial results, explanations, failed routes and contribution tools. The separate plectis repository publishes reusable software components with local checks. This packet carries the published papers and reading material from both repositories. Reading a proof or receipt is not rerunning it.
do_not_confuse: 88 components and 103 paper modules are different inventories: components are runnable/public claim units; paper modules are explanatory subsystem records. They are not one-to-one.
A paper is exposition. Checked Lean source is proof authority; the Lean claims registry owns public claim status; this build ran no Lean kernel.
The doctrine carried here is the complete public doctrine projection, not private raw seed or every internal doctrine record in ai_workflow.
Repository maps are counted, hash-bound depth-two topologies. They avoid embedding thousands of repeated path prefixes; follow public_tree_url for an exact leaf outside the named entrypoints.
